### `kill_engine` ignores a reserved but not yet published engine generation

* **ID:** f-20260914-23 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src-tauri/src/chess.rs:458 (`kill_engine` checks published actors only), `prepare_engine_search` / `get_best_moves_core`
* **Defect:** When `prepare_engine_search` has reserved generation G2 but not yet published it, Kill Engine returns success; `get_best_moves_core` can then publish and run G2 after the user asked for the engine to stop.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/engine-lifecycle.md` and `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md`: a cancel must reach work admitted before it, or the stop is not a stop. Related: the ledger entry "Unscoped stop prefers a pending admission and leaves the live search running" covers `stop_engine`, not `kill_engine`.
* **Open question:** Does a kill cancel reservations (so G2 never publishes), or wait for publication and then terminate — and how is that ordering proven for the reservation window?
* **Found by:** `review-engine-protocol` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 93, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `67941e1b`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.
* **Handled 2026-10-07** (drain session 803e3b54-ecf6-42cb-a06a-c289c0600244, drain run 80fae550-0102-4ac3-83d7-2a39c45de07d, retired after Grok's balance ran out, then interactive Claude Code takeover; adopted reviewed plan `tasks/plans/2026-10-07-kill-engine-reserved-generation.md`; review history `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-07-f-20260914-23-review.md`; decisions `d-20261007-16` through `d-20261007-19`, `d-20261007-20` superseded by `d-20261007-21`).
* **Answer to the open question:** cancel the reservation (`d-20261007-16`). Kill flags the admitted generation under the registration and admission-coordination barrier, so a reserved generation can no longer publish or `go`, and a later `consume_engine_search` of it returns `Error::Cancellation` (`d-20261007-18`). Kill does not take the lifecycle lock. A published actor is handed to the shared pending reap (`handoff_published_locked`), stays in `pending_actors` until that task finishes, and the shared task is the only `EngineActor::terminate` (`d-20261007-19`); Kill also joins every other pending actor of its key (`d-20261007-21`). `chess::kill_engine` delegates to `EngineSupervisor::kill_engine`.
* **Correction-introduced defects fixed in this run:** a stale exact stop no longer reaps an actor a newer warm search reused; a cancelled interactive start that fails with `EngineDisconnected` returns `Cancellation` while a failed reap stays `OperationAndCleanup` (one shared `cancelled_search_error`); `kill_engines` (board-tab close) now awaits a report analysis reap that is already in `pending_actors` and returns its failure (`terminate_analysis_engines` through `kill_engine`).
* **Commits:** `366dc0a4` (fix), `d59c4837`, `8dd299cc`, `2cc3e83e`, `6ccf4600`, `33f0130a`, `5cc62fab` (review and gate repairs), decisions `b2cf9b26`, `f592a7f9`, `d3779f71`, `910995da`, handoffs `7665c9fe`, `5a50ed65`. Pushed `5a50ed65`.
* **Known limits:** an admission inserted after Kill released the publication barrier is a later search, not a tombstoned key (same class as `f-20260915-07`). `get_engine_logs` returns no logs for an actor that is mid-reap in `pending_actors`. Out of scope as planned: `stop_engine`, `terminate_tab`, game-engine keys, `f-20260915-06`, `f-20261006-04`, `f-20261001-14`.
* **Proof:** full `cargo test --bin chessfable` 2017 passed; regressions `kill_engine_*`, `kill_engine_command_cancels_reserved_generation`, `stale_exact_stop_leaves_reused_actor_published`, `terminate_analysis_engines_waits_for_pending_reap_and_keeps_failure`. Final `pnpm gates:push -- --rust` green on `5a50ed65` (`artifacts/gates/20261007T131940678Z-3309618`). CI run 37627921509: rust-windows-test, rust-macos-test and rust-platform (windows msvc, macos x86_64, macos aarch64) success. Local install `5a50ed65` provenance reviewed.

### A failed cleanup of a new PGN export file after registration failure is discarded

* **ID:** f-20260914-24 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:2421 (`create_pgn_export_destination` best-effort `remove_file`)
* **Defect:** If registering a freshly created export destination fails and removing that file also fails, the removal error is discarded and only the registration error returns, leaving an unregistered file at the path the user selected.
* **Why it matters:** The user is told export failed while a stray file remains at their chosen path; `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md`.
* **Open question:** How is a primary error plus a failed compensation reported — a combined error variant, an applied-despite-error result, or a persisted cleanup record?
* **Found by:** `review-error-handling` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 92, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `97c29add`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.
* **Handled 2026-10-07 (drain run a28f99b3-2237-4fa8-b5ca-715d97e8cd6a, session 8b3d897d-692d-409e-a374-dbda0b7c61e8).** Both `create_pgn_export_destination` arms in `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` now pass the `remove_entry_at` result to one classifier, `pgn_export_error_after_cleanup`. A successful unlink, an already-missing leaf, or an unlink whose parent sync is uncertain returns the registration error unchanged; the uncertain case logs one export-specific warning. Any other removal failure, including an identity mismatch with a replaced leaf, returns `Error::with_cleanup(primary, Err(removal))`. A primary `CommittedDurabilityUncertain` still skips rollback. There is no new error variant, wire message, renderer change or persisted cleanup record. Decision `d-20261007-22`. Note on the Where line: the original `mod.rs:2421` pointed at `keep_adopted_handle`; the discarded removal was the `let _ =` in both cfg arms.
* **Commits:** `cb9a0516` fix and tests; `0d63aa89` names the PGN-file dialog grant policy (`PGN_FILE_DIALOG_GRANT_TTL`, `PGN_FILE_DIALOG_GRANT_USES`) at both arms and `main.rs` `issue_pgn_workspace_blocking`, a review-code-quality finding in the same area; `ebd934cd` source pin requires the removal result to be the classifier's direct argument in both arms. Records: `e5755bfc` decision, `a29bc3cb` plan-review handoff `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-07-f-20260914-24-review.md`.
* **Rejected:** applied-despite-error, a persisted cleanup record, reporting a parent-sync-uncertain unlink as a cleanup failure, folding the raw removal result the way workspace-file rollback does, and merging with `engine_image_error_after_cleanup` (see `d-20261007-22`).
* **Known limits:** when unlink really fails, the stray file stays; the change is that the user is told cleanup also failed. Windows is proven by the source pin, `pnpm rust:windows:check` and CI only; there is no Windows removal injector. A crash between create and return is unreported (engine-image analogue `f-20261004-12`). `f-20261004-24` (compensation inside `create_regular_at` before an identity exists) stays open and reuses this reporting answer.

### A header-only game followed by another header block is indexed as one game

* **ID:** f-20260914-25 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** pgn-import · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src-tauri/src/pgn.rs:491 (a header starts a new game only after `has_movetext`)
* **Defect:** The byte-offset indexer starts a new game at a header only once movetext has been seen, so `[Event "empty"]\n\n[Event "B"]\n\n1. e4 *` is indexed as a single range although the parser reads two games; offsets then disagree with game numbering.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/pgn-scanning.md`: game-boundary detection and the cached byte-offset index must agree with the parser.
* **Found by:** `review-pgn-index` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 99, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `97c29add`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.
* **Handled 2026-10-23:** Commit 0bb7bfd9 replaces the movetext-only split condition with a header-block terminal state. Blank separators and semicolon comments after a started game end its header block, while percent escape lines do not. A subsequent valid header starts a new exact byte range even when no moves preceded it. Adjacent headers, inline tag pairs, quoted braces and multiline brace comments keep their prior behavior. Decision d-20261023-08 rejects splitting on repeated tag names or changing the vendored parser.
* **Proof:** Eight `pgn_scanner_pickup` tests pass, comparing the production scanner with the actual vendored pgn_reader and checking exact ranges under LF/CRLF and BOM/no BOM. The pinned fixture changed from one [0, 37) range to [0, 17) and [17, 37), agreeing with the parser's two games. Semicolon and percent cases also compare against the parser, including unmatched braces in ignored lines. Independently removing the header fix and the semicolon correction with exact source-only git patches made their retained tests fail with exit 101, and restoration returned the suite to exit 0. Existing preface test passes. Pre-review checks pass, including Windows GNU clippy, which is compile proof only. Logs, patches and statuses are under `/tmp/chessfable-f-20260914-25/`. Final review, gates and release follow this source closure.
* **Attribution:** The sensitive Codex leaf used gpt-6.1-sol high. Plan authorship and arbitration shared one root context. Detection ran in fresh Codex sessions on the same OpenAI model family as the code. No novel product question or additional finding was filed.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"close","effect_lines":3,"effect_sha256":"54ebc57ab9f9a592eb95e4b86c422e1c989562864bf80d0115b334cbd48f526a","header_sha256":"70a47488f3589f4e60293b4ceda2a982b9d2a116a843ed20a03d47b39f17b339","header_status":"handled","input_sha256":"0e9cd15906ddbc0af312504e9c793919e4490eddc2c28c1b4364183f7513bdcf","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"fe4a3ecb83b3f7bf0193db26d5a3fded0daba02bd73c04c03fc64478387d4312","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260914-25"],"target":"f-20260914-25","v":1} -->

* **Reopened during push review 2026-10-23:** The source closure above is superseded pending correction. Fresh correctness and PGN-index lenses traced three additional scanner/parser disagreements: a percent line after a blank separator makes the parser treat the next tag as movetext, an indented percent line ends the parser's headers, and an indented tag line ends headers before a later unindented tag. The first case is introduced by 0bb7bfd9, while the indentation cases predate it. The fix is not released. Keep the handled BOM and invalid-preface joiners closed, since those proofs remain valid. The current run will reproduce and repair the shared boundary mechanism before push. Raw reports are `/tmp/chessfable-f-20260914-25/lens-correctness-r1.txt` and `lens-pgn-index-r1.txt`.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"set-header","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"a586b4a5f4ae7e634894dd6c8a1659b171321e31961857c02b6fb0c00d5b41b5","header_sha256":"70a47488f3589f4e60293b4ceda2a982b9d2a116a843ed20a03d47b39f17b339","header_status":"handled","input_sha256":"1355b5f0bf63498133e3eccdf6a7869ff48a0b6e5903bf8144d85d17fd4f4f66","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"817d9c14a2a9020375fad58da90f4b03a992a5ece286070f85c2ac8432dae22d","options":{"headers":{"Status":"open"},"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260914-25"],"target":"f-20260914-25","v":1} -->

* **Entry revalidation 2026-10-23:** lens → build. Push-review counterexamples and the fresh read-only source probe show that universal agreement with the current parser conflicts with established scanner acceptance tests. The scanner deliberately preserves boundaries across percent escape lines and quote-aware comment shields, while the vendored parser consumes an escape line's terminating newline and does not accept indented header continuation. A local emulation of all parser quirks would regress existing scanner contracts. The original blank-header fix alone is therefore insufficient to settle the shared header-boundary contract. The BOM repair and invalid-preface closure remain valid.
* **Open question:** How should scanner indexing and the vendored parser share correct header-boundary behavior for whitespace and percent escape lines while preserving existing scanner acceptance, exact offsets, limits and streaming behavior, without copying parser quirks into another state machine?
* **Evidence and proof:** `/tmp/chessfable-f-20260914-25/probe-boundary-r1.txt` traces the production scanner tests and parser phases. The build must reproduce the three review counterexamples against both real implementations, preserve all existing scanner tests, and run the vendored parser tests plus the affected Rust and contract gates. New evidence qualifies d-20261023-08's original rejection of a parser rewrite, rather than authorizing a wholesale rewrite. The preferred candidate is a bounded correction to parser header whitespace and escape-line newline consumption, with no new public API or grammar framework.

### Threefold detection after `appendMove` walks the selected variation instead of the main line it appended to

* **ID:** f-20260914-28 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** chess-tree · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src/state/store/tree.ts:697 (`appendMove` appends to the main line), :769 (repetition walk follows `state.position`)
* **Defect:** With main line `Nf3 Nf6 Ng1 Ng8 Nf3 Nf6 Ng1`, a side variation selected at `[1]`, and `Ng8` appended to the main line, the initial position has occurred three times but the result stays `*`, because the repetition walk follows the selected side variation rather than the path the move was appended to.
* **Why it matters:** A drawn game is not declared; `.claude/rules/chess-tree-semantics.md` (mainline-vs-variation assumptions).
* **Found by:** `review-chess-semantics` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 94, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `93b36669`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.
* **Pickup closure (2026-10-23):** Already fixed by published commit `e91b191288baf9c9990ff0cc74d300ccc230a7c4` (`Correct tree navigation, repetition, and PGN semantics`). At pickup HEAD `c4da644fe6ae269457164b44dcd5fd44593fffb5`, `appendMove` calls the shared move mutation with `last: true`, which derives `position` from the mainline endpoint and passes that path to `isThreeFoldRepetition`. The repetition walk uses that argument rather than the selected `state.position`, so selecting a variation no longer changes which history is counted.
* **Proof:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/state/store/tree.test.ts` passed all 124 tests, including `appendMove checks repetition along the mainline append path`. That regression appends the eighth knight move with the cursor at the root and asserts a draw. The selected-variation case is supported by the current source path, not claimed as a separately executed fixture. Retained command and completion evidence: `/tmp/chessfable-side-lane-astra-20261023/gate-repetition-proof.92R3SS/`.
* **Scope and attribution:** This pickup changes only the finding record. No replacement implementation, new product decision or source edit is needed. Plan authorship and arbitration share the root context. Detection runs in separate Codex review sessions in the same OpenAI model family as the code. Push review and release proof follow this closure.

### Windows PGN cache revision uses creation time as ctime, so a same-length in-place rewrite keeps stale offsets

* **ID:** f-20260914-29 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs:181
* **Defect:** On Windows, revision tracking substitutes `creation_time()` for ctime. An in-place, same-length rewrite that restores the last-write timestamp leaves identity, size, mtime and creation time unchanged, so stale game offsets stay trusted (a cached two-game file rewritten as a padded one-game file still returns the old second range).
* **Why it matters:** Wrong games are served from a stale index on Windows; part of the Windows port.
* **Open question:** Which Windows change signal is trustworthy for cache revision (USN journal, `FILE_ID_INFO` plus `ChangeTime` from `FileBasicInfo`, or content hashing), and what does it cost on large PGNs?
* **Found by:** `review-pgn-index` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 97, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `0fd2dbed`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.

* **Handled 2026-09-18 (next-finding, executor DeepSeek Flash, full auto):** Windows `pgn_snapshot_file` now fills `ctime_nanos` from inline `GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileBasicInfo).ChangeTime` on the already-open handle (`2a23c0b6`). Query failure is `Error::Io`; no `creation_time` fallback. Unix `st_ctime` and `opened_file_change_stamp` unchanged. Tests: same-length rewrite restoring last-write must miss (`same_length_rewrite_restoring_mtime_misses_offset_cache`); source pin via `body_at_indent` (`698b7e8c`). Decision `d-20260918-14`. Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-18-f-20260914-29-review.md`. Runtime proof of the Windows `ctime_nanos` assertion is `rust-windows-test`. Left open: `f-20260917-04`, `f-20260917-13` (blocked on `f-20260905-10`), `f-20260916-10`.

### Engine retirement failures during workspace deletion are logged and discarded

* **ID:** f-20260914-30 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** src-tauri/src/file_workspace.rs:1255-1262
* **Defect:** A workspace deletion that succeeds on disk returns success even when retiring the engine processes or executable registrations it owned fails; the failure is only logged, so engines or registrations may remain active with no error surfaced.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md`: every exit path is cleaned up or reported truthfully. Distinct from the inbox entry about workspace creation post-commit errors (filed the same day).
* **Open question:** After a committed delete, is a retirement failure returned as an applied-despite-error outcome the renderer acts on, retried, or recorded for startup reconciliation?
* **Found by:** `review-error-handling` cumulative diff review lens (Codex), 2026-09-14, confidence 98, during the `f-20260830-06` slice-1 build run (range `950f2e1d..16476781`). Pre-existing (originating commit `dc6b7841`), outside that run's area, so deferred; not reproduced in that run.
* **Handled 2026-10-07** (Claude Code, drain session 1abd5112-6a94-4620-b2d7-eca2aa0bfc34, drain run a28f99b3-2237-4fa8-b5ca-715d97e8cd6a; adopted reviewed plan `tasks/plans/2026-10-07-workspace-delete-retirement.md`, plan review in `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-07-f-20260914-30-review.md`).
  * **Open question answered** (`d-20261007-23`): returned, not retried and not recorded for startup. When the blocking delete succeeded, a failed `retire_executables` now returns `Error::PartialRemoval { removed_entries, cause }` with the retirement error as `cause` after a `diagnostic()` warn; category `partial-removal`, which the renderer already maps to applied-despite-error and answers with a relist and the generic confirmation. When the blocking delete already failed, that error is returned unchanged (never re-wrapped through `CommittedRemoval::finish`) and the retirement failure is logged.
  * **Count** (`d-20261007-24`): `remove_workspace_entry` returns `(CommitDurability, usize)`; the `usize` counts the registry ids this call removed that an earlier failed save had not already removed. Database and puzzle removal discard it.
  * **Superseded:** the "Unlink success stays Ok; terminate failure is logged" clause of `d-20260901-29`, through `d-20261007-25`, which restates that entry's surviving clauses.
  * **Commits:** `9604efbd` (fix + tests), `eb9b9503` (Files page test for the structured `partial-removal` relist), `eebbca1c` (cumulative-review round 1: count documented and named, shared retired-executable assertion, walk-cause diagnostic asserted).
  * **Proof:** nine named cargo tests green (`--bin chessfable`; the crate has no lib target); revert proofs staged by the write leaves: the old Ok-after-log swallow fails `retirement_failure_after_committed_delete_is_partial_removal`, counting `removed_ids.len()` fails `remove_workspace_entry_count_excludes_pending_unpersisted_removals` (3 vs 2), swapping the kept walk cause fails `walk_partial_removal_survives_retirement_failure`. `pnpm rust:windows:check` green; Windows and macOS runtime remain with the CI `rust-windows-test` / `rust-macos-test` jobs.
  * **Known limit, unchanged:** the OS process may still be alive after the error returns; the session tombstone is in memory only. Trash, restore and database/puzzle retirement (`f-20260917-08`) are out of scope.

### On macOS no engine can start: the executable and every resource lease are passed as `/proc/self/fd/N`

* **ID:** f-20260914-31 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:821` (`EngineResourceLease::uci_value` returns `/proc/self/fd/{fd}` under `cfg(unix)`), `:1049` (`EngineExecutable` launch path `/proc/self/fd/{fd}`), `:1065-1066` (the documented interpreter-script re-exec via that path), `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs:261` (spawn relies on it); Linux-only test harnesses in `src-tauri/src/chess.rs:1861`, `src-tauri/src/game.rs:3379` and `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:7943-7947` read `/proc/self/fd`.
* **Defect:** the engine launch and UCI resource options are built on Linux procfs. macOS has no `/proc`, so spawning any engine fails with `NotFound` and every resource value handed to `setoption` names a path that does not exist. Observed on the real macOS runner in CI run 34866102377 (`rust-macos-test`, commit `6544ca56`): `engine::process::tests::{inherited_resource_fd_survives_path_replacement_for_uci_child, real_child_ignoring_quit_is_force_killed_within_reap_budget, spawn_owns_the_stderr_drain_until_terminate}`, `infra::path_authority::tests::{engine_resource_leases_pin_files_and_directories, inherited_descriptors_cover_every_resource_lease_and_the_engine_image}`, `game::tests::{game_engine_initialization_passes_resource_provenance_to_actor_logs, game_engine_is_registered_while_uci_initialization_is_pending}` (timeout), `chess::tests::{get_best_moves_core_wires_resource_options_through_production_flow, report_core_restores_child_resource_provenance_after_fresh_resolution}` ("resource engine did not reach its log barrier"). The `rust-macos-test` job stays red for this finding.
* **Why it matters:** Felix decided on 2026-09-12 that ChessFable ships on macOS; without a launch path the app cannot analyse on macOS at all. The descriptor-pinning invariant (a replaced executable or resource cannot be launched after authorisation) must survive the port.
* **Open question:** what replaces `/proc/self/fd/N` on macOS while keeping the pinned-inode guarantee — `/dev/fd/N` (on macOS opening it duplicates the descriptor and shares its offset, and an interpreter script re-opening that path after `exec` loses a close-on-exec descriptor), `posix_spawn` of a verified path with an identity re-check, or passing resources as inherited descriptors with a different UCI value — and how are the Linux-only test harnesses made platform-neutral?
* **Related:** `f-20260830-06` (parent; slice 1 made this observable), follow-up (f) "Windows engine directory resources, archive install and executable mode" (inbox `20260914-053235-3130471`), plan-review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260830-06-slice-1-review.md` (load before review).
* **Found by:** the `rust-macos-test` CI job added by `f-20260830-06` slice 1, run 34866102377, 2026-09-14; source trace by the slice's orchestrator (grep of `/proc/self/fd` uses). Not reproduced locally (no macOS runtime on this machine).

* **Handled 2026-09-15 (macOS engine-launch build run):** macOS now launches engines from pinned descriptors. Every launch flow (interactive analysis, report analysis, `get_engine_config`, game engines) goes through `resolve_launch`, which admits first, resolves leases under the path-authority lock on the blocking gateway, collapses duplicate options last-wins, and clones the executable and every effective file resource from the held, authorised descriptor into `engine-launch/<uuid>` (0o700, owned by an `flock`), with `fclonefileat` and a `pread` copy fallback on `EXDEV`/`ENOTSUP`. File resource values are the pinned leaf paths; directory resources are sent as `getpath(held)` and verified against the actor's held leases before any `setoption`. Linux keeps procfs values. The shell harnesses named in `Where` run on every Unix target and fall back to the plain value when it is not a procfs path; `inherited_descriptors_cover_every_resource_lease_and_the_engine_image` stays Linux-only because it tests the Linux inherited-descriptor mechanism itself, and macOS has its own pinned-leaf and directory-verification tests. Decision `d-20260915-02`; review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-macos-engine-launch-review.md` (16 plan rounds, 7 diff rounds, 3 post-push CI rounds). Code `3878a6a9`, `1e884b2b`, `ba539255`, `20d69da4`, `1ad9513e`, `42dbac5b`, `638839dc`, `dbcabea6`, `c8aaef6c`, `98124bf1`, `6ecd1ac8`, `6ae152e2`. Proof: CI run 34974674436 on `d0c698ff`, `rust-macos-test` green, with the nine Unix tests of this finding's original failure list (the tenth, `inherited_descriptors_cover_every_resource_lease_and_the_engine_image`, is now Linux-only by design; `inherited_resource_fd_survives_path_replacement_for_uci_child` runs as `authorized_resource_survives_path_replacement_for_uci_child`) and every new macOS-runnable test in the range reporting `ok`, including `report_core_restores_child_resource_provenance_after_fresh_resolution`, whose intermittent macOS failure exposed the search-read race fixed in `6ecd1ac8`.

### On macOS, listing a directory removed during enumeration returns success instead of `NotFound`

* **ID:** f-20260914-32 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs` `read_directory_entries_at` end-of-stream check (`fstat(dir)` then `if directory_stat.st_nlink == 0` → `NotFound`, around line 107-114); test `infra::fs::tests::read_directory_entries_at_refuses_a_removed_directory` (~line 2275).
* **Defect:** removal of the held directory during enumeration is detected only by `st_nlink == 0`. On the real macOS runner (CI run 34866102377, `rust-macos-test`, commit `6544ca56`) the test that opens a directory, removes it and enumerates the held descriptor did not get `Error::Io(NotFound)`, so on APFS the removed directory still reports a non-zero link count and the listing returns success. The `rust-macos-test` job stays red for this finding.
* **Why it matters:** workspace and database listings would present a snapshot of a directory that no longer exists instead of refusing it, which the Linux path deliberately refuses (`f-20260905-05` descriptor-relative enumeration). The slice-1 port of the walker (`f-20260830-06`) preserved identity, no-follow and mount refusal on macOS but not this invariant.
* **Open question:** which signal proves on APFS that a held directory descriptor refers to a removed directory — `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` failing, `openat(dir, ".")` returning `ENOENT`, `fstatat` of the parent-relative name, or `getattrlist` — measured on a real macOS runner before choosing, and does the chosen signal also hold for the recursive-delete and install walks?
* **Related:** `f-20260830-06` (parent), plan-review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260830-06-slice-1-review.md` (load before review), decision `d-20260914-07` (the shared `Dir` walker).
* **Found by:** the `rust-macos-test` CI job added by `f-20260830-06` slice 1, run 34866102377, 2026-09-14. Not reproduced locally (no macOS runtime on this machine).

* **Handled 2026-09-15 (macOS engine-launch build run):** one shared post-walk check, `ensure_directory_not_removed`, now runs after the walk of each held directory in `read_directory_entries_at`, `sync_tree` and `remove_tree_at`. Non-macOS Unix keeps `st_nlink == 0`; macOS compares `getpath(dir)` with `fstat(dir)` by device and inode (`held_matches_path`), treating `ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR` or a mismatch as removed, while a directory renamed away stays live. Listing keeps cancellation precedence; install refuses a source removed mid-walk; recursive delete reports the removal. This answers the open question for the recursive-delete and install walks as well. Decision `d-20260915-01`; review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-macos-engine-launch-review.md`. Code `506891a8` (plus the `target_os = "macos"` alignment in `ba539255`). Proof: CI run 34974674436 on `d0c698ff`, `rust-macos-test` green, with the originally failing `read_directory_entries_at_refuses_a_removed_directory` and every new removal, replacement and install/recursive-delete walk test reporting `ok`.

### A dialog selection under a symlinked ancestor is granted and then refused at promotion

* **ID:** f-20260914-33 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` `grant_dialog_operations` (stores `NativePath::from_path(path)` unchanged after `validate_dialog_target`, which uses `fs::symlink_metadata` and therefore follows ancestor symlinks), `promote_dialog` → `validate_target` → the no-follow ancestor walk `open_dir_no_follow` in `src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs`; production callers `issue_file_workspace_blocking` (`src-tauri/src/file_workspace.rs`), `issue_pgn_workspace_blocking` (`src-tauri/src/main.rs`), and the in-authority grant inside the PGN creation path (`mod.rs`, `self.grant_dialog_operations(` near the `canonical_operations(EntryPurpose::PgnFile)` call).
* **Defect:** the grant step accepts a pathname whose ancestor is a symlink, but every later step walks the stored pathname with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` and refuses it with `ENOTDIR`. A user who picks a file or folder through a symlinked directory (macOS `/tmp` and `/var`, a symlinked home or data directory on Linux) gets a grant that can never be promoted or used. Observed on the real macOS runner in CI run 34862122222 (`rust-macos-test`, commit `8b98a870`): about 370 tests failed with `Io(NotADirectory)` at `promote_dialog` because `tempfile::tempdir()` lives under the `/var` symlink; the CI job now sets `TMPDIR=$RUNNER_TEMP` (commit `6544ca56`), which hides the fixture symptom but not the production path.
* **Why it matters:** the authority already binds legacy database paths to their canonical parent (`canonical_binding`, test `database_file_target_binds_a_symlinked_ancestor_to_its_canonical_parent`), so the same user selection is accepted through one door and unusable through another. On macOS, where Felix decided on 2026-09-12 that the fork ships, symlinked system directories make this reachable from an ordinary file dialog.
* **Open question:** should every acquisition door (dialog grant, legacy migration, PGN creation) canonicalise the parent once at acquisition through the existing `canonical_binding` so the stored pathname is symlink-free, or should the no-follow walk start from a canonicalised ancestor at use time — and which of the two keeps the ancestor-swap guarantee the no-follow walk exists for (`nofollow_rejects_ancestor_and_final_parent_symlinks_and_temp_collision_retries`)?
* **Related:** `f-20260830-06` (parent port), `f-20260905-10` (ancestor-symlink window in app-data bootstrap — a different door), `f-20260912-11` (canonical pathname carried by `DatabaseFileTarget`).
* **Found by:** Claude Code orchestrator source trace of CI run 34862122222, 2026-09-14, during the macOS runtime build run. Reproducible on Linux with a symlinked ancestor; not yet reproduced by a test.

* **Handled 2026-09-15 (build run, session a680a996):** every caller-supplied acquisition door now stores a symlink-free spelling proven by a no-follow descriptor walk (`acquire_target`, shared with `database_file_target`); promotion re-proves; PGN export creation is descriptor-relative and bound to the named parent's identity; descriptor-verified registrations keep their spelling (`d-20260915-03`). A failed promotion consumes its dialog grant (`d-20260915-04`). Code: `2b640767`, `50db4e10`, `ffddee3e`, `86ab3738`, `78287a7c`, `5cd3b559`; records `bd0b725a` (`f-20260915-03`), `9e342f6f`, `f3553c86`. Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260914-33-review.md` (7 plan-review rounds, 65 issues; 4 diff-review rounds). Successors: `f-20260914-36` (R1-06, R3-05, R3-06), `f-20260915-03` (D1-01).

## 2026-09-14 — filed through the inbox spool

### A spawned engine whose publication is aborted is terminated by an untracked task that shutdown does not await

* **ID:** f-20260914-34 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs` `impl Drop for PendingActorGuard` (around line 1351): when the guard still holds an actor, it moves it into `tokio::spawn(async move { actor.terminate().await … })` and returns. Reached when `spawn_registered` has spawned the child but publication is aborted before registration (admission cancelled by tab close, retirement or shutdown, or an initialization error).
* **Defect:** the termination and reap of that child run in a detached task with no owner, no join handle and no registration the shutdown path walks. Tab shutdown and application exit terminate only registered actors; if the runtime is torn down before the detached task runs, the child is neither terminated nor reaped, and its termination error surfaces only as a log line. This contradicts `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` ("Leave a spawned process … whose removal depends on the happy path" is a DO NOT) and the engine-lifecycle rule that a canceled late actor is reaped.
* **Why it matters:** engine children outliving the application is the incident class of issue #723 (`e5422566`) and `f-20260830-51`; this is the remaining unowned path. The macOS engine-launch plan (`tasks/plans/2026-09-14-macos-engine-launch-and-removed-dir.md`, round 4, R4-04) relies on this reap for its cancellation guarantee.
* **Open question:** should aborted-publication termination be owned by the supervisor (a pending-termination set that tab shutdown and `RunEvent::ExitRequested` await with the existing bounded deadlines), or be performed inline by the caller of `spawn_registered` on its error path before returning, and how is the `Drop` backstop then reduced to a logged invariant violation?
* **Related:** `f-20260830-51` (app exit terminates nothing deterministically — handled), `f-20260830-53` (detached stderr reader — handled), `f-20260914-31`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` plan lens (round 4, confidence 91) during the macOS engine-launch build run, 2026-09-14; source verified by the orchestrator. Not reproduced by a test.
* **Handled 2026-10-06** (drain session a1330039-2a64-416c-babe-3eee05aac68a, adopted reviewed plan `tasks/plans/2026-10-06-aborted-publication-termination-owner.md`; plan review `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-06-f-20260914-34-review.md`). Open question answered with option (a), `d-20261006-16`: the supervisor owns every spawned, unpublished actor in a pending set keyed by admission generation (entered in `initialize_admitted_actor` and `start_interactive_search`'s fresh-actor branch, moved into `actors` under the same `admission_coordination` section that publishes it). Each entry has one entry-owned termination task (`d-20261006-19`) started by the first owner (inline rejection, drain or dropped `PendingActorGuard`) and awaited by the others; every owner receives the failure through the new internal `Error::Shared` (unchanged payload and bindings). `terminate_all`, `terminate_tab` and `retire_matching` share one `drain_matching` over registered and pending actors, so exit and tab close await the child and aggregate its failure with key and generation. The `Drop` backstop is not reduced to a log (it would leak the child, against `d-20260927-07`). `RegistrationGuard` unchanged (`d-20261006-17`); exact single-generation paths unchanged (`d-20261006-18`, owned by `f-20260914-23`).
* **Commits:** `d0021b46` (fix), `acae7397` (review repairs: log wording, named test scenarios, shared V3/V4 scenario, unix fake-engine anchor for the interactive fresh-actor branch), `df56aad8` (`PathAuthority::open_for_engine_test` test constructor), `7d3d6fe0` (decisions), `c9c8fa7d`/`0eebe4b0` (review record).
* **Proof:** V1–V8 plus `fresh_interactive_dropped_publisher_exit_awaits_child_termination`; with the pending drain disabled, V1, V2, V2b, V3, V4, V5 and V8 fail, and the interactive test fails without fresh-branch tracking. `cargo test` 1974 passed.
* **Rejected:** inline caller termination with a logged `Drop` (leaks on a dropped future); a `TaskTracker` (cannot be scoped to a tab or engine); independent `terminate()` calls per owner (a losing caller reports `Ok`).
* **Left open elsewhere:** spawn after the final drain is `f-20261006-04`; remaining fixture copies in `game.rs`/`chess.rs` filed to the inbox.

### An engine-configuration probe stays registered until application exit when its command is dropped after publication

* **ID:** f-20260914-35 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/chess.rs` `get_engine_config`: `spawn_registered(…, collect_engine_configuration)` publishes the probe under a unique `EngineKey("engine-config", <uuid>)`, and only the normal path afterwards calls `state.engine_supervisor.terminate_exact(&key, supervised.generation)`.
* **Defect:** if the command future is dropped after publication and before `terminate_exact` (renderer reload, webview teardown, or any future cancellation of the command task), nothing terminates the probe: its key belongs to no tab, so tab close never reaches it, and it stays an idle engine child registered in the supervisor until application exit. `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` requires cleanup on every exit path, including cancellation.
* **Why it matters:** each abandoned probe keeps an engine process (and, on macOS after `f-20260914-31`, its materialised launch leaves) alive for the rest of the session.
* **Open question:** should the probe's termination be owned by a drop guard held across the `spawn_registered` → `terminate_exact` span (which then needs an owned asynchronous termination, the same design question as `f-20260914-34`), or should configuration probing run inside a supervisor-owned operation whose cancellation terminates the probe?
* **Related:** `f-20260914-34` (unowned termination of an aborted publication), `f-20260901-14` (config probe moved under the supervisor — handled).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` plan lens (round 5, confidence 93) during the macOS engine-launch build run, 2026-09-14; source verified by the orchestrator. Not reproduced by a test.
* **Handled (2026-10-06, drain session 242e290f-6c04-4b2d-b232-29a2961c45f0, adopted reviewed plan `tasks/plans/2026-10-06-published-generation-guard-handoff.md`, review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-06-f-20260914-35-review.md`):** `spawn_registered` now returns the armed `RegistrationGuard` of the generation it published (`initialize_admitted_actor` no longer disarms it on success), so every caller owns the generation by type. `get_engine_config` (through the new crate-private `get_engine_config_core`) terminates its probe with `guard.terminate_now()`; a drop at any await — including while that termination is pending — leaves the guard armed and its `Drop` terminates exactly that generation. Game construction takes the returned guard instead of constructing a second one. Commits `7338a676` (guard handoff, V1–V4 tests, main.rs source scan), `a6a075de` (analysis review repairs), `8fee1eff` (game spawn helper dedup). Decisions `d-20261006-20` (the open question: the caller-owned drop guard, not a supervisor-owned probing operation — `d-20260927-03`), `d-20261006-21` (slice with `f-20260926-03`).
* **Proof:** `config_probe_abort_during_termination_removes_generation` aborts the probe once the fixture shows `quit` and asserts no `engine-config` generation remains registered and the child exited; reverted to the old `terminate_exact` path it fails by assertion. Full `cargo test --locked`: 1980 passed.
* **Rejected:** re-arming a fresh `RegistrationGuard` in each caller (second and third copy of one ownership step, rule 11); a supervisor-owned probing operation (`d-20260927-03` rejected an `OperationLease` wrapper).
* **Review:** plan 4 rounds (I1, I2 fixed). Cumulative diff review: 10 Codex code lenses + records lens; 4 Fix (unreachable `None` arm, duplicate failure helper, game spawn conversion duplicated, missing post-termination test) + 1 records Fix, all closed in closure round r2; 1 Defer to the already-filed `f-20260926-04` (`finish_analysis_failure` flattens diagnostics); 1 Skip (wording nit on `d-20260927-03`).

### Path-authority entries already persisted under a symlinked-ancestor spelling stay unusable for descriptor-relative operations

* **ID:** f-20260914-36 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` registry load (`PathAuthority::open_with_clock`, the `for mut stored in registry.entries` loop near `:2458-2520`) and `refresh_entry` (`:5844`), which deserialise and validate a stored `NativePath` verbatim with the ancestor-following `validate_target`; the refusing use-time walks are `infra/fs.rs` `open_verified_parent` / `open_verified_directory` (via `workspace_mutation_target`, atomic replacement).
* **Defect:** the fix for `f-20260914-33` binds newly acquired pathnames to their canonical parent, but an entry persisted before that fix (a PGN workspace, PGN file, download destination or engine resource selected through `/tmp`, `/var` or a symlinked home) keeps its symlinked-ancestor spelling. `refresh_entry` still marks it `Available`, while every descriptor-relative mutation refuses it with `Io(NotADirectory)`; re-selecting the same object creates a second entry beside it because the reuse lookups compare spellings lexically.
* **Why it matters:** the user sees an available workspace that cannot be written; Windows/macOS/Linux porting (`f-20260830-06`, Felix 2026-09-12) makes symlinked system directories an ordinary selection.
* **Open question:** rebind such entries at registry load (in memory, persisted at the next commit) only when the canonical binding proves the same identity through the parent descriptor — and if so, how is a rebinding failure surfaced (mark unavailable, keep available and log, or report through the availability API) — or migrate them once with a registry schema bump, or leave them and tell the user to re-select?
* **Related:** `f-20260914-33` (the acquisition-time fix; plan-review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260914-33-review.md`, issue R1-06, load before review), `d-20260912-04`, `d-20260912-05`.
* **Found by:** Codex plan lenses review-minimalism, review-tauri-security, review-root-cause, review-tests and review-error-handling (round 1, confidence 89-99) during the `f-20260914-33` plan review, 2026-09-14: load-time rebinding was proposed and cut as outside that finding's mandate.

* **Annotated 2026-09-14 (f-20260914-33 plan review, round 3; status stays open):** two use-time doors are the same class and belong to this finding's design. (1) `database_file_target` (`src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` ~`:3990`) compares only the re-acquired identity with the stored one, not the canonical path: after `real/x.db3` is stored, replacing `real` with `real -> moved` lets it mint a carrier bound to `moved/x.db3` (same inode) — review-correctness, confidence 98, issue R3-05. (2) `workspace_root` (~`:4584`, used by `set_active_database_root` / puzzle / engine) validates the stored root with ancestor-following `validate_target`, so an ancestor swapped between acquisition and activation still commits the active root, which the next no-follow `resolve` refuses — review-root-cause, confidence 97, issue R3-06. Enforcing path equality at use time would refuse legacy entries persisted under a symlinked-ancestor spelling that work today, so the choice (rebind at load, then enforce equality at use) is this finding's open question, not f-20260914-33's. Plan-review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260914-33-review.md`.
<!-- ledger-meta {"command":"annotate","effect_lines":1,"effect_sha256":"cb53c1cd56619f399c41c08541df23d5f0061af55fec32f2b2929b714ccff588","input_sha256":"5278733684530f72e3ad62c82352d6064af5a21c3e613a954ba56bd14f8e7046","kind":"mutation-receipt","operation":"df5267bb6176eb5ea17e18ffbf88ff96a6942536493efb36b15201938c9c11af","options":{"section":null},"request_id_sha256":null,"results":["f-20260914-36"],"target":"f-20260914-36","v":1} -->

* **Handled 2026-09-18.** `refresh_entry` now decides availability on the canonical spelling, and a
  post-construction pass (`rebind_legacy_spellings`) re-proves every non-exempt legacy entry through
  the existing `acquire_target` primitive, adopts the canonical spelling in memory and commits once.
  A refusal leaves the entry `Unavailable` with its stored spelling and one `log::warn!` naming the
  entry, and never fails startup; a hard commit failure keeps the in-memory rebinding, which the next
  ordinary commit flushes. `recover_pending_artifacts`, which runs immediately after, now skips and
  logs an undecodable stored path instead of propagating it. Entries whose spelling is deliberately
  raw are exempt — the six `AppOwnedDefaultRoot` directories under the `AppDataDir` and anything
  below them, plus `PathClass::AppOwnedRoot` — because `get_or_create_root` (`mod.rs:4790-4806`) and
  `cleanup_engine_images` (`:6060`) compare those spellings lexically; a path carrying a `ParentDir`
  component is never exempt. The app-data context reaches the authority through `open_for_app`,
  because the load loop refreshes every entry before `open` returns; the existing constructors are
  unchanged.
* **Commits:** `93f6acf3` (the change), `cbd2df92` (the launch-root argument on every target),
  `1d1404d7` (diff review round 1), `72db1ac0` (two stale doc references).
* **Split out, with the measurement that forced it:** path equality at `database_file_target`
  (R3-05) and `workspace_root` (R3-06) were approaches B and C of this plan through round 3 and are
  now `f-20260917-13`, blocked on `f-20260905-10`. Three rounds measured that enforcing equality
  unconditionally refuses a database child registered in the same session, while exempting the
  app-owned subtree stops `database_file_target` enforcing it for exactly the entries R3-05 is
  about. Also filed: `f-20260917-12` (an unavailable persisted active root is indistinguishable from
  none, so the app silently substitutes a fresh default workspace).
* **Rejected alternatives, each on a measurement:** a stored `descriptor_bound` flag (incomplete —
  `register_database_child` builds a `StoredEntry` directly at `mod.rs:5513`, and no flag can
  classify entries written before it existed); containment in a `PathClass::AppOwnedRoot` entry
  (vacuous in production — `main.rs` passes `vec![]` and `AppOwnedRoot::new` is `#[cfg(test)]`);
  `starts_with(AppDataDir)` alone (the pickers accept arbitrary paths inside that tree); a
  `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump; and no exemption at all.
* **Known residual, owned by `f-20260905-10`:** a user can pick a folder or file inside one of the
  six app-owned directories and is then exempted with the application's own entries. It is not
  distinguishable by pathname, and separating it means giving up the lexical reuse above.
* **Review:** 13 plan-review rounds (all seven lenses APPROVED) and 2 cumulative-diff rounds
  (eight lenses, all APPROVED). Record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-17-f-20260914-36-review.md`.
  Windows criterion 14 compiles only under `cfg(windows)`; its runtime evidence is the CI
  `rust-windows-test` job.

### Live analysis accepts a pending result from an engine that was unloaded while the search ran

* **ID:** f-20260914-37 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** result-not-bound-to-its-process · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/boards/EvalListener.tsx`, `isCurrentAttempt` (around line 222) and the `onBestMoves` / search-result handlers that call it.
* **Defect:** `isCurrentAttempt` checks that the component is mounted, that the attempt is the active, uncancelled one, that the request fingerprint (tab, close revision, FEN, moves, settings, engine id and handle or URL) is unchanged, that analysis is enabled, that the game is not over, and that the tab exists and is not closing — but not that the engine is still present in the engine list and `loaded`. If an engine (notably a remote one) is unloaded while its result is pending, the result can resolve before the passive unmount cleanup runs and still update the evaluation cache and progress.
* **Why it matters:** this is the incident class `03826167` ("results from unloaded engines were still consumed", cited in `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` and `engine-lifecycle.md`), which requires a payload to be used only while its engine is loaded.
* **Related:** `f-20260831-09` and `f-20260903-01` (same root, handled: results bound to tab, position and process).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` plan lens (round 8, confidence 92) during the macOS engine-launch build run, 2026-09-14; source read by the orchestrator, not reproduced by a test.

* **Handled 2026-09-18** in `c099a471`. Entry revalidated at `lens`; confirmed in source: unloading an engine commits to the jotai store before React runs the passive unmount cleanup, so `mounted.current` is still true in that window. `isCurrentAttempt` now reads `enginesAtom` and requires a `loaded` entry whose executable identity (`engineIdentity`: type, id, handle or URL — extracted and shared with the request fingerprint) equals the attempt's. Covers both the remote promise path and the native `best_moves` broadcast. Proof: two new tests in `EvalListener.test.tsx` unload the engine outside `act` (store written, component still mounted) and resolve the result; both red without the fix, green with it. Lens: `review-engine-protocol` on the DeepSeek executor, APPROVED. Rejected: relying on unmount cleanup (the window is the defect) and a render-time ref of `engine.loaded` (only updates on render, same window).

## 2026-09-15 — filed through the inbox spool

### A trailing line from a finished search can be consumed as the next search's result

* **ID:** f-20260915-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** result-not-bound-to-its-process · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs`, `service_search_read` (the request-id check before reading, around line 3032) and the actor state transition to idle on the first `bestmove`.
* **Defect:** the request id is checked only before a read starts. After search G1's first `bestmove` sets the runtime idle, output that G1 still emits — a delayed `info` line or a duplicate `bestmove` — stays in the pipe untagged. If the caller then sends `position`/`go` for search G2, that old line is read inside G2's search and can be taken as G2's result.
* **Why it matters:** `engine-lifecycle.md` forbids binding a response to the most recent request because it arrived after it; a result from G1 attributed to G2's position is the stale-result class of `4e8d10b0` and `03826167`.
* **Related:** `f-20260914-37`, `f-20260831-09`, `f-20260903-01` (same root).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` diff lens (confidence 94) during the macOS engine-launch build run, 2026-09-15. The lines blame to `17fac36f`, `97c29add` and `e4e0f8d3`, before that run; source read by the orchestrator, not reproduced by a test.

* **Handled 2026-09-18** in `6a0a74cc`. Entry revalidated at `lens`; confirmed reachable: `game.rs` sends `position` then `go` with no ready barrier, so a line a finished search emitted after its `bestmove` was read inside the next search. Fix in the actor, the single `go` choke point: `EngineRuntime` marks every started search's output unsynchronized, and `start_search` sends `isready` and discards everything up to `readyok` before `go` while the mark is set. Only an idle `readyok` clears it, so `chess.rs`'s explicit `ensure_ready` saves the second round trip and one taken during a live search does not count. Proof: `trailing_output_of_a_finished_search_is_not_the_next_searchs_result`, updated `replacement_waits_for_old_bestmove_before_go` and `cancellation_during_a_pending_search_read_stops_and_allows_a_new_search` (which had pinned the duplicate `bestmove` being adopted) red with the barrier disabled; `a_ready_barrier_during_a_search_does_not_close_its_output` red with the idle guard removed; engine::process module 110/110 green. Lens: `review-engine-protocol` on the DeepSeek executor, APPROVED. Rejected: tagging lines with request ids on read (UCI output carries no id, so the read has nothing to compare) and a barrier only in `game.rs` (every caller would have to remember it).

### A destroyed webview does not stop a silent report analysis search

* **ID:** f-20260915-02 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/chess.rs`, `analyze_position_with_owner` (`proc.next_line_cancellable(&supervised.cancelled)`); `src-tauri/src/main.rs`, `cancel_destroyed_window_operations` (the `WindowEvent::Destroyed` handler).
* **Defect:** report analysis reads search lines cancellably only against `SupervisedEngine::cancelled`. Destroying the webview cancels the report's operation ticket through `OperationRegistry::cancel_owner`, which cancels the operation token but never sets that flag. While the engine emits no line, the read keeps waiting, so the child keeps searching until the search deadline (ten minutes) with no `stop` and no reap. `cancel_analysis` is unaffected because it sets the flag through `cancel_exact`.

That marks the exact generation's supervised cancellation flag, which next_search_line_cancellable observes every 25 ms even when no engine line arrives. Other owners remain active.
* **Proof:** the root reran cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked --bin chessfable -- native_window_operation_wiring_tests through agent-gate. Exit 0, six tests passed, including lifecycle_cancellation_signals_the_exact_supervised_analysis, destroyed_window_core_cancels_held_worker_but_not_other_owners and the shared signal source pin. No code change was needed for this stale finding. Proof log: gate-phase-proof.UB9EmK under the run gate directory.

## 2026-09-15 — filed through the inbox spool

### Resolution proves a persisted entry's leaf identity but not its parent's, so a replaced parent holding a hard link passes

* **ID:** f-20260915-03 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` `retained_workspace_target` (and the other use-time resolutions built on `open_verified_parent` / `open_verified_directory`: `workspace_mutation_target`, `database_file_target`, `resolve`), which walk the stored spelling no-follow and compare only the leaf `(dev, ino)` with `StoredEntry.identity`; the registry stores no parent identity.
* **Defect:** after an entry for `dir/ws/game.pgn` is persisted, replacing `dir/ws` with a different real directory that contains a hard link to the same `game.pgn` inode passes every use-time check (no symlink is met, the leaf identity matches). Descriptor-relative writes that create siblings — the `.info` sidecar, atomic-replacement temporaries, SQLite `-wal`/`-journal` files — then land in the replacement directory, not the one the user selected.
* **Why it matters:** the no-follow walk exists so a persisted capability names the selected location; a parent swap with a hard link keeps the leaf object but redirects every sibling write. Requires write access to the parent's parent, so it is a same-user or shared-directory attacker, not a remote one.
* **Open question:** should the registry persist the parent directory identity at acquisition (a `StoredEntry` schema change with a migration for existing entries, which cannot be recovered for entries persisted before it) and have every use-time resolution compare it, or is the leaf identity plus the no-follow walk the accepted boundary, documented as such?
* **Related:** `f-20260914-33` (acquisition-time canonical binding; review record `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-14-f-20260914-33-review.md`, diff-review issue D1-01), `f-20260914-36` (use-time validations of persisted entries that compare identity only — R3-05 is the same identity-only comparison in `database_file_target`), `f-20260830-09` (unlink by name).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-tauri-security` diff lens (confidence 98) during the `f-20260914-33` build run, 2026-09-15. Source read by the orchestrator; not reproduced by a test.
* **Why rejected:** Parent-directory swap needs a same-user local attacker who already owns the user's files; never observed. Not worth fixing under universal rule 4d (only a defect with a cost is a finding; setup cleanup 2026-10-13).

### Opening the engine workspace sends the raw opener diagnostic, which can carry a native path, to the renderer

* **ID:** f-20260915-04 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** bindings-ipc · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/main.rs:1615-1631` (`open_engine_workspace_blocking`): `.map_err(|error| Error::InvalidInput(format!("cannot open engine workspace: {error}")))`; serialisation `src-tauri/src/error.rs` — `Error::InvalidInput` carries its owned message into the renderer payload (pinned by `error::tests::invalid_input_serializes_the_owned_message`, `:816-828`).
* **Defect:** the `tauri_plugin_opener` error is formatted into an `InvalidInput` string, and `InvalidInput` is the one variant whose message crosses IPC verbatim. An opener failure that quotes the resolved engine-root path or an OS diagnostic therefore puts native path text into the renderer, which the path authority exists to keep out (`engine_root_path` is resolved in the backend precisely so the renderer never sees it).
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` — never move a raw backend diagnostic into the renderer; the crate already maps comparable failures to opaque variants (`Error::TauriOpener` is categorised `Platform`, `error.rs:265`).
* **Fix shape:** return the opener failure through the existing opaque variant (`Error::TauriOpener` or an `Io`-style fixed-text mapping) so the payload carries only a category, and add a serialisation test that an opener error containing a path does not appear in the payload.
* **Found by:** `review-tauri-security` plan lens (Codex retry), 2026-09-15, confidence 94, during the `f-20260914-07` plan review; the orchestrator verified the `map_err` and the `InvalidInput` serialisation at source. Outside that run's area, so deferred. Not reproduced with a live opener failure.
* **Implementation review update (2026-10-14, drain session 88354097-6004-4014-a60b-919fe79440ef):** Root source tracing found a portability gap in the newly added opener regression. The test compares the supplied opener path to the raw temporary-directory spelling. PathAuthority::registration_target calls acquire_target, whose Unix branch uses canonical_binding to canonicalize the parent, and workspace_root returns that admitted canonical spelling. A legitimate alias in the temporary-directory ancestors therefore makes the new assertion fail even though the production opener receives the correct authorized root. This is relevant to ordinary macOS /var ancestor aliases. A focused alias-path run is next, followed by the same native worker's test repair if the assertion fails. No production authorization widening is proposed.

## 2026-09-15 — filed through the inbox spool

### Interactive engine command may wait for EOF after `bestmove`, holding a live engine until the ten-minute timeout

* **ID:** f-20260915-05 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/chess.rs:599` (reported; the interactive read loop after `bestmove`).
* **Defect (reported, not verified):** after `bestmove` the loop keeps reading until EOF; a conforming UCI engine stays alive after `bestmove`, so the command would wait for the ten-minute timeout before cleanup.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/engine-lifecycle.md` / `async-resource-invariants.md` — every async operation needs a terminal state that does not depend on the child exiting.
* **Found by:** `review-engine-protocol` plan lens (Codex retry), 2026-09-15, confidence 99, during the `f-20260914-07` plan review, which does not touch engine code. Outside that run's mandate and area; not read line by line — verify the loop and its terminal condition before fixing. Checked against open `engine-uci` findings: not a duplicate of `f-20260911-03` (stop deadline) or `f-20260915-01` (trailing line).
* **Why rejected:** Pickup on 2026-10-23 confirms the reported EOF dependency is a false positive. `EngineProcess::next_line` delegates to the actor's request-aware `next_search_line`. `service_search_read` sets `EngineState::Idle` when it dequeues `bestmove`, and the next request returns `Ok(None)` before reading stdout because that request is no longer searching or stopping. This terminates `process_interactive_search_output` even while the child remains alive. The delegation, idle transition and terminal request guard all date to `97c29addc`, before this report was filed.
* **Proof:** On pickup HEAD `1056b7552721e625a87605d9f5859b677eef4d4e`, three `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin chessfable` filters passed: `warm_interactive_searches_reuse_resource_handles_and_publish_each_generation` (1 test), `interactive_producer` (4 tests), and `eof_is_disconnect_not_empty_success` (1 test). The first drives the actual command core through three searches using one real child, with one UCI initialization and three `go` commands. The fixture remains in its input loop after `bestmove`. The EOF test separately proves EOF is an error rather than the successful terminal `None`. Retained log and exit-0 completion: `/tmp/chessfable-side-lane-astra-20261023/gate-engine-terminal-proof.9eYBBm/`.
* **Scope and policy:** Preserve the warm-process lifetime chosen in `d-20261005-14` and the trailing-output barrier in `d-20260918-16`. No source edit or new design decision is needed. Plan authorship and arbitration share the root context. Detection runs in separate Codex review sessions in the same OpenAI model family as the code. Records review and release proof follow this rejection.

### `terminate_tab` releases admission coordination without a closed-tab marker, so an in-flight admission can publish an engine for a closed tab

* **ID:** f-20260915-07 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs:1373` (reported; `terminate_tab`).
* **Defect (reported, not verified):** `terminate_tab` releases admission coordination without recording that the tab is closed; a new admission can insert while registration is held, then publish after the close scan and create an engine for the closed tab.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/engine-lifecycle.md` — a result and a process must stay bound to the tab that asked; a process for a closed tab has no owner to reap it. Related to `f-20260914-23` (`kill_engine` and a reserved generation), which concerns a different entry point.
* **Found by:** `review-engine-protocol` plan lens (Codex retry), 2026-09-15, confidence 88, during the `f-20260914-07` plan review. Outside that run's mandate and area; not read line by line — reproduce the interleaving before fixing.
* **Why rejected:** Pickup on 2026-10-23 traces the reported native-only interleaving through the production caller and finds no closed-tab engine publication path. `BoardsPage.closeTab` sets `closingTabsAtom` before its first await and retains the marker through native teardown and removal of tab metadata. The `EvalListener` subscription synchronously cancels its active attempt. Its sole production local-search path checks that attempt before preparation and again after preparation returns, before dispatching `getBestMoves`. A preparation that enters native admission after the close scan therefore returns to a cancelled attempt and is stopped or released without starting an actor. A search already dispatched has an existing reservation, which `terminate_tab` cancels under the registration and admission-coordination barrier. A consumed lease retains that cancellation through publication and reaps a late actor.
* **Governing decision:** `d-20260908-04` already chooses transient native admission cancellation plus synchronous renderer close intent and rejects permanent closed-tab tombstones. The relevant renderer cancellation and native barrier date to `67941e1b9`. Current tab-presence validation also prevents a removed tab from restarting after the close marker is cleared. A failed close may start a fresh search for the still-live tab, as intended. The report omitted the renderer half of this existing protocol. No new design decision or source change is needed.
* **Proof:** On pickup HEAD `37f31d5877b8cf2c5d1d5c4e9c33425605eb113b`, both `EvalListener.test.tsx` and `BoardsPage.test.tsx` passed, 115 tests total, including close during predecessor stop, close during preparation, tab removal, failed-close recovery, and marker retention through metadata removal. The Rust test `tab_close_cancels_consumed_admission_and_reaps_late_actor` also passed and verifies exact cancellation, one late-actor termination and preservation of the other tab's reservation. Commands, logs and exit-0 completion are retained under `/tmp/chessfable-side-lane-astra-20261023/f-20260915-07/gate-tab-close-proof.TCNKOb/`.
* **Scope:** This rejection does not close the separate application-exit ownership question in `f-20261006-04`. Plan authorship and arbitration share the root context. Detection runs in separate Codex review sessions in the same OpenAI model family as the code. Records review and release proof follow this rejection.

### The test workflow's branch filter `"*"` skips every branch whose name contains a slash

* **ID:** f-20260915-08 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** ci-workflows · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `.github/workflows/test.yml:3-8` — `push: branches: ["*"]` and `pull_request: branches: ["*"]`.
* **Defect:** GitHub's `*` branch pattern does not match `/`, so a push or pull request on a branch such as `feature/foo` runs no job of the test workflow at all — no linter, no boundary checks, no coverage ratchets, no Rust platform jobs. Measured indirectly on 2026-09-15: the throwaway branch `probe/windows-rust-test` ran only because its own copy of the workflow named it explicitly (GitHub run 34995837526); the `f-20260914-07` plan-review lenses (review-plan 99, review-root-cause 99, review-tests 99) confirmed the pattern semantics. No checker in `scripts/` reads the value, so a change to it is unguarded either way.
* **Why it matters:** every gate the repository documents as running "on every push" silently does not for slash-named branches; `d-20260830-20` forbids a gate that reports success without checking, and here the gate does not report at all.
* **Fix shape:** use `"**"` for both filters (or drop the filters), and add a clause to an existing workflow-contract checker (`check-gate-routing.mjs` or `check-tool-version-parity.mjs`) that pins the trigger, with its staged failure recorded; decide whether pull requests from every branch are wanted.
* **Found by:** `review-plan` and `review-root-cause` plan lenses (Codex), 2026-09-15, rounds 3-4 of the `f-20260914-07` plan review; cut from that plan as outside its mandate (review-plan 90, review-tauri-security 96).
* **Why rejected:** No slash-named branch is ever pushed; only master. Not worth fixing under universal rule 4d (only a defect with a cost is a finding; setup-findings triage 2026-10-13).

### The Windows refusal pins guard the 40 known sites but nothing pins the shared refusal helpers or catches a new unlisted refusal

* **ID:** f-20260916-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/platform_support.rs` — the helpers `refusal` (`:3-5`, private), `unsupported` (`:7-9`), `unsupported_plural` (`:11-13`), `off_unix_refusal` (`:15-21`); the row tables `refusal_guards_are_first_statements_and_precede_their_effects` (`:184-353`) and `non_unix_counterparts_have_only_typed_refusal_bodies` (`:361-487`); the whole-tree scans `refusal_text_has_one_source` (`:489-514`) and `routed_refusal_labels_are_unchanged` (`:516-715`). * **Defect:** after `f-20260914-07` every one of the 40 Windows refusal sites is pinned exactly and those pins run on Windows, but three gaps remain, each of which lets a Windows refusal change or disappear with every gate green: (1) the shared helpers and the refusal constant have no pinned declaration — an effect added inside `refusal`, or a changed format, body or visibility, leaves every row's text unchanged; (2) nothing ties the row tables to the set of refusals that actually exist, so a **newly added** refusal site (or one spelled through an alias, a bare `Error::Conflict` literal or the constant) is simply unlisted and unpinned; (3) the callees on an effective non-unix path (`single_leaf`, `validate_components`) are unpinned, so an effect added inside one of them precedes a refusal without changing its row. The row loops are also fail-fast, so one broken row hides the rest.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` and `d-20260914-05` — a Windows refusal is the only thing keeping an unported path from bypassing the identity and no-follow invariants; these are the routes by which one stops refusing without any test going red.
* **Open question:** how is a closed-world assertion over the refusals staged at all, given that its own assertions live in `infra/platform_support.rs` and push-review-policy §2 forbids staging by editing the artefact under test — move the scan into a separate checker with its own fixtures (a checker whose inputs are scratch files can be staged), pin the helpers from a *different* module's test, prove completeness at a different level (a compile-time registry the refusal helpers themselves populate), or accept named argued assertions? This finding owns the inherited issue IDs **R4-02** (closed-world completeness), **R11-01** (staged evidence for the visibility pin) and **R15-01** (the forbidden own-source staging route), plus the stated limitations R6-06 (split or alternately spelled refusal literals are undetected) and R14-03 (duplicate-row and exact-count paths are argued, not staged).
* **Found by:** the `f-20260914-07` plan review, rounds 4-15 (review-plan, review-tests, review-root-cause, review-error-handling, review-tauri-security, review-minimalism on Codex; confidences 88-99), split out under rule 12a on 2026-09-16 because the class did not converge inside that mandate.

* **Annotated 2026-09-16 (f-20260914-07 plan review round 16; status stays open):** the split is narrower than first filed. Round-16 lenses (review-plan 99/97, review-tests 99) showed that the helper, constant and callee pins are *not* separable: an effect inserted into `off_unix_refusal`, `refusal`, `single_leaf` or `validate_components`, or a changed `UNSUPPORTED_DIRECTORY_ENUMERATION` literal, changes the refusals of the existing 40 sites, which is `f-20260914-07`'s own mandate. Those pins therefore returned to that plan (revision r17), together with the row-collecting failure reporting the staged matrix needs; the constant and the two callees are staged as ordinary production mutations, while the four helper-body and declaration pins are recorded as **argued, not staged**, because reaching them requires editing `infra/platform_support.rs` itself (push-review-policy §2 forbids that staging route).
* **What remains this finding's work:** the closed-world completeness assertion — tying the G/B row tables to every refusal occurrence in the tree so that a **future** unlisted, aliased or differently spelled refusal (a new `#[cfg(not(unix))]` site, `use … as`, a bare `Error::Conflict` literal, a `concat!`-split message) cannot exist unpinned — and the design question of how such an assertion is staged at all when its own code lives in the file it scans. Inherited issue IDs are unchanged: **R4-02**, **R11-01**, **R15-01**, plus the limitations R6-06 and R14-03. Load `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-16-f-20260914-07-review.md` before planning.

## 2026-09-16 — filed through the inbox spool

### Windows component validation accepts an NTFS alternate data stream in a path leaf

* **ID:** f-20260916-02 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `validate_components` (`src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:3130-3153`) and `single_leaf` (`src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs:1534-1541`); the consuming walk is `resolve_windows` (`src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/resolved.rs:803`). Both function bodies are pinned byte-exactly by `check_helper` in `src-tauri/src/infra/platform_support.rs:1150-1170`.
* **Defect:** `validate_components` rejects `/` and NUL only under `#[cfg(unix)]` and has no Windows branch, so a component such as `existing.db3:stream` passes validation. On Windows that names an NTFS alternate data stream rather than a child entry, so a renderer-supplied filename can address a different native object than the authority validated. `resolve_windows` opens the final child before any leaf-level check, so rejecting only in `single_leaf` would be too late.
* **Why it matters:** the path authority exists to make a renderer-supplied name address exactly the object it was authorised for. Today the gap is unreachable because the Windows filesystem paths refuse first; it becomes reachable the moment the Windows port lands (`f-20260914-10`).
* **Open question:** where is the colon rejected so that `resolve_windows` cannot open a stream first — in `validate_components`, in `single_leaf`, at the resolver, or a shared predicate used by all three — and how are the two `check_helper` pin strings updated in the same commit so the all-platform refusal assertions stay consistent (`d-20260916-01`)?
* **Related:** `f-20260914-10` (the Windows atomic-replacement port, which makes this reachable and from whose plan this was cut as out-of-mandate). Raised by `review-root-cause` (95) and `review-tauri-security` (91/99) in rounds 3-4 of that plan review, which held that fixing it inside that slice violates its A6 slice boundary.
* **Found by:** `f-20260914-10` plan review rounds 3-4 (review-tauri-security, review-root-cause, review-minimalism on Codex), 2026-09-16; source-verified by the orchestrator at the lines above.

**Handled 2026-09-17** by the `f-20260914-09` Windows database port, commit `cd3132dd`, under the
scope amendment that slice's mandate carried: it may not ship a route that makes this reachable and
leave it open.

**Why it became this slice's problem.** `create_database_child` takes a **renderer-supplied**
filename, and its only filter — in `create_workspace_database_blocking` (`main.rs:1058-1060`) —
rejects `/`, `\` and emptiness. Enabling database creation on Windows therefore put
`existing.db3:stream` on a live renderer-driven route into `open_windows_child`, which is stronger
reachability than the dialog-selected paths this finding was originally filed against.

**The answer to the open question — where the colon is rejected — is: in one cfg-free predicate,
routed through both gates.** `windows_component_refusal(name) -> Option<&'static str>`
(`infra/path_authority/mod.rs`) is *called* only where the Windows path grammar is active but is
*compiled and unit-tested everywhere*, which is what makes it assertable at all: a
`#[cfg(windows)]` validation branch cannot be exercised by a Linux test. It is routed through
`validate_components` **and** `single_leaf`, because `single_leaf` is the last gate every Windows
caller passes and `validate_components` is not on every route — a rule placed only in the latter
would not have held for persisted or dialog-selected paths.

It rejects a component containing `:`, `/`, `\` or NUL; a component over 255 UTF-16 units
(the NTFS/ReFS maximum); a trailing dot or space, because Win32 strips both when resolving a
non-verbatim path and the port deliberately hands SQLite a non-verbatim path; and a reserved DOS
device stem — `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9`, `LPT1`-`LPT9` and the superscript
`COM¹`-`COM³` / `LPT¹`-`LPT³` aliases — with or without an extension, because `NUL.db3` resolves to
the device.

**Both `check_helper` pin strings changed in the same commit**, which is the mechanism working as
designed rather than an obstacle. A separate rule bounds a database leaf at 250 units at both entry
points, `create_database_child` and `register_database_child`, so the derived `.ecsi` sidecars stay
inside the component limit instead of being accepted at creation and refused at every later search.

**Proof:** the predicate is unit-tested on Linux over `a:stream.db3`, over-length names, `a/b`,
`a\b`, NUL, trailing dot and space, and each device stem, plus a test that both gates route through
it. No Windows runtime evidence exists for any of it (`f-20260917-02`); the Windows-target
`cargo check --all-targets` and `clippy -D warnings` are green.

**Related:** closed together with `f-20260916-03` (the `u16` truncation in the same helper) and
`f-20260914-09`. Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-09-17-f-20260914-09-review.md`.
