### Move comments are rendered as Markdown and each comment ends the notation row, so clock-annotated games read one move per line and "59. text" becomes a numbered list

* **ID:** f-20261001-10 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/common/Comment.tsx` (comment text goes through `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`; a comment with several non-empty lines switches to `display: block`), `src/components/common/notationRows.ts` (~339-383: every move comment is emitted as its own `comment` row via `addComment`, which closes the current move row).
* **Defect:** in Felix's game Beck–Riewe (Elo Vierer Caissa Center, 2026.08.09, `~/Documents/Sport/Schach/ChessFable/Eigene Partien/Meine Partien.pgn` line 2178) almost every move carries a comment with the remaining clock minutes (`6. Nf3 {62} h6 7. Be3 {59. Olvidé mi preparación. Tengo Ld3 en mi prep.} Bd6 8. Be2 {59}`). Two effects, both visible in the database preview and the analysis tab: (1) the comment `59. Olvidé…` starts with "number + period + space", which Markdown parses as an ordered list starting at 59, rendering a block-level list with margins and an empty gap; ChessBase/PGN comments are plain text, so any comment opening with `12. `, `- `, `# ` or `> ` is restyled; (2) because each comment ends the row, a game where nearly every move has a short comment collapses to one half-move per line and wastes most of the panel width.
* **Fix shape:** decide whether PGN comments are Markdown at all (they are written by ChessBase and other tools as plain text; the Annotate editor is a rich-text editor whose output format must be checked before changing the reader); at minimum disable the block constructs (lists, headings, blockquotes) for comment rendering. Let short single-line comments stay inline in the move flow instead of forcing a row break. Pixels via `pnpm test:e2e:container`.
* **Open question:** are PGN comments Markdown at all, given what the Annotate editor writes back, and which comments may stay inline in the move flow instead of ending the row.
* **Why `build`:** the Markdown question interacts with the Annotate editor's write format (round-trip), and the row model change touches `notationRows.ts` shared by every notation view.
* **Found by:** Felix, session e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984, 2026-10-01 (screenshot of the analysis tab).
* **Closed (handled 2026-10-13, drain session 92629247-30b0-484a-a451-64fd78836bcb, full auto, adopting the reviewed plan):** both effects are fixed in the notation and in the Annotate editor. (1) PGN comments are an inline-only dialect: every block construct (`12. `, `- `, `# `, `> `, rules, tables, footnotes, code) and raw HTML stay literal text; bold, italic, strike, `++underline++` and links render. The notation and the editor parse comments with one shared `marked` lexer (`src/utils/commentMarkdown.ts`, `createCommentMarkdown()`); `Comment.tsx` renders its tokens itself (react-markdown and remark-gfm removed); `++` underline follows one rule, `COMMENT_UNDERLINE` in `src/utils/pgnComment.ts`, so chess `Qh7++ Kh8 Qg8++` stays text; the editor lost its heading/quote/rule/list controls and never writes blank-paragraph sentinels, unescaped link titles or unrepresentable underline. (2) A move comment no longer ends its notation row in any inline move run (inline view and the table view's variation runs); a variation's starting comment travels with its move; navigation scrolls the current move's own cell into view when its row is taller than the viewport; the table view's black-move variations are read from the right parent. Commits (pre-push, oldest first): `d4552d8b` (phase 1), `90e3cb60` (phase 2), `7d018df7` (phase 3, new container snapshot `files-inline-comment-prose-files-preview.png`), `db2f547d`, `0525eb8c`, `19637ced`, `2d27b27d`, `d86f368c`, `2bb5f752` (review repairs), `e56b16e2` (phase 4, shared lexer), `c944289e` (coverage mapping), `c00ccd0d` (editor serialization repairs). Decisions d-20261013-09..17 (09, 10, 14, 15, 16 superseded in part as recorded). Review: 4 plan-review rounds by the planner, 5 diff-review rounds plus two focused review-plan judgments, all in `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-13-comment-dialect-and-inline-flow-review.md`. Proof: per-phase vitest, lint:ci, i18n:check, checks:pre-review and test:e2e:container green (final gates in the push). Rejected: a length threshold for "short" comments, keeping block Markdown, keeping two parsers in step by patches, removing underline authoring. Deferred: the editor's general save losslessness for literal delimiters next to authored marks and adjacent links (pre-existing tiptap behaviour, needs an escape-contract decision and an owned serializer) — filed through the inbox as a `build` finding that loads the handoff above.

### Games are split across a Files page and a Databases page by storage format, not by what the games are for

* **ID:** f-20261001-11 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** the sidebar routes to `src/components/files/FilesPage.tsx` (PGN files in the workspace folder, typed game/repertoire/tournament/puzzle/other via `src/components/files/file.ts`) and `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` (SQLite `.db3` collections built by `convert_pgn`, `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs:727`; Lichess/Chess.com account sync always writes a database, `src/components/home/AccountCard.tsx:156`).
* **Observation:** Felix (2026-10-01) asked why his own played games ("Meine Partien", 116 games) live under Databases while his opening files live under Files: "in chess space this is all in one list. This is all the same structure. Whether I use my games or an opening preparation." The split is inherited from En Croissant. Technically it is justified — PGN files are editable documents (variations, comments, repertoire practice), databases are indexed copies for position search, player/tournament views, deduplication and the opening-explorer reference — but the UI exposes the storage format as two top-level places, and a user thinks in purposes ("my games", "my Caro-Kann prep").
* **Open question:** how a single library list composes the database detail pane and the file card, and what happens to the two existing routes, once Felix chooses an option below.
* **Decision:** Should ChessFable show one library of everything that holds games — databases and PGN files in a single list, each with a type badge and the actions that fit it — instead of two separate sidebar pages?
  * **(a) One library view.** One sidebar entry; one searchable list with type badges (Games database / Repertoire / Study / Tournament / Puzzle); selecting an item shows the matching detail pane (database stats + Explore, or the file card); storage stays exactly as it is (PGN files stay files, `.db3` stays SQLite) and "Add" offers both "import as database" and "create file". Costs: a new page that composes both existing panes, one merged search/filter, and the two old routes kept as redirects; every Files/Databases e2e snapshot changes.
  * **(b) Keep two pages, explain them.** Rename to purpose-based labels (e.g. "Studies & repertoires" / "Game collections"), add a one-line description on each page and cross-links. Costs: cheap; the split itself stays, so "my games" vs "my prep" still means knowing which format each was imported as.
  * **(c) Keep as is.** No cost; the confusion Felix hit stays for every user.
  * **Ruled out:** converting everything to one storage format. Turning repertoires into databases loses free-form editing and the repertoire practice mode; turning databases into PGN loses indexed position search and the opening explorer over large collections (Mega Database). The formats are right; only the presentation is in question.
  * **Recommend:** (a), because it matches how chess players organise material (ChessBase shows one database window for games and openings, Lichess one study list) and removes the "where did my games go" question at its source, while keeping both technically correct storage formats. Against it: it is the largest of the three, it diverges further from upstream En Croissant's navigation (harder to compare against upstream history), and the two detail panes have quite different actions, so a merged list must make clear why a database row offers "Explore" and a file row offers "Open/Practice".
  * **Product impact:** changes where a user finds and opens their games and repertoires — one place instead of two sidebar pages — and what the sidebar shows.
  * **Session:** e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984 — transcript
    `~/.claude/projects/*/e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984.jsonl`
* **Decision made:** (a) one library view, as phase 1 of 'one library + linked collections': one Library sidebar entry replacing Files and Databases, one searchable list of files and databases with type badges, detail pane by item type, /files and /databases redirect; phase 2 (every collection exists once, the PGN file is the truth, linked search index) is filed as its own finding — Felix: in chess space this is all in one list; users think in purposes, not storage formats. Chosen 2026-10-04 after the recommendation was reviewed and approved by the orchestrator and four Codex lenses (review-plan, review-root-cause, review-minimalism, review-pgn-index) over four rounds.
* **Closed (handled 2026-10-13, drain session fab6795c-3780-4adc-8356-6d9441cd768f, full auto, adopting the reviewed plan):** phase 1 of the chosen option (a). One Library sidebar entry and `/library` overview list PGN workspace entries and SQLite databases in one roving-focus tree with one search, one type filter (the PGN categories plus "Games database"), type badges and one kind-qualified selection; the detail pane follows the selected kind (file card and file actions, folder summary, database settings/stats/Explore/actions, or the error pane); "Create file", "Create folder" and "Import or download database" sit side by side. `/files` and `/databases` redirect to `/library`; the explorer stays at `/databases/$databaseId`, and the sidebar still resumes an active explorer. Storage is unchanged. Commits (after rebase): `bb296f33` (Library composition, extracted `useFileWorkspace`/`useDatabaseLibrary`, routes, e2e, 38 container baselines, verify:app harness, coverage scope), `09226589` (type-filtered folder test, stale comments), `7141711a` (wrapping buttons keep their label centred; Explore was 15 px off), `1cfffd88` (coverage mapping), `b372db43` (review handoff `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-13-unified-library-review.md`). Decisions d-20261013-01..05 and d-20261013-08 (supersedes d-20261001-08's single `/databases` match path). Proof: full `pnpm gates:push -- --frontend` green at `b372db43` (contract, coverage, bundle, full container e2e, frontend mutation), `pnpm verify:app` green at `09226589`, required CI green on `b372db43`, installed `b372db43`. ### The renderer's tree keeps only 26 glyphs, so ChessBase's `$8` (□) and `$11` (=) render as an empty grey badge and are deleted on the next save

* **ID:** f-20261001-12 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** chess-tree · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/utils/chess.ts:451` (`node.annotations.push(NAG_INFO.get(token.value) || "")` — every NAG outside `NAG_INFO` becomes `""`), `src/utils/chess.ts:452` (the sort puts `""`, nag 0, first), `src/utils/chess.ts:79` (`if (annotation === "") continue;` — the writer drops it), `src/utils/annotation.ts:40` (`NAG_INFO` maps `$7`→□ and `$10`→= but not `$8` or `$11`), `src/components/boards/Board.tsx:473` + `AnnotationHint.tsx` (the board badge draws `annotations[0]`; `""` has colour gray and an empty glyph), `src/state/store/tabStorage.ts:30` (the persisted schema is the same 26-value enum).
* **Defect:** Felix's ChessBase-exported repertoire files (`~/Documents/Sport/Schach/ChessFable/Repertoire/*.pgn`) contain `$8` 2,021 times and `$11` 380 times (all other NAGs in them are understood: `$1 $2 $5 $6 $14 $15 $16 $17 $18 $19`). (1) A move carrying `$8` or `$11` shows a grey dot with no symbol in the corner of its destination square (observed 2026-10-01 on `7. d4 $8` in `Weiß_Königsgambit.pgn`). (2) Saving the game back — to the PGN file or to a database through `write_db_game` — writes the renderer's PGN, which omits every `""`, so every `$8`/`$11` in the saved game is deleted without warning. (3) Because `""` sorts first, a move with both an unknown and a known NAG shows the grey dot instead of the known symbol. The database itself stores NAGs losslessly as raw `$n` strings (`src-tauri/src/db/encoding.rs`, `encode_nag`), so the loss is entirely in the renderer's tree model.
* **Open question:** how the tree stores NAGs losslessly (raw NAG numbers versus glyph aliases), how the Annotate panel's toggles treat alias NAGs (`$7`/`$8` both □, `$10`/`$11` both =), what an unknown NAG shows, and how open tabs persisted in the old 26-glyph shape migrate.
* **Why `build`:** the fix changes the tree node's annotation type, its persisted schema and every consumer; Felix asked for a Codex plan review before implementation.
* **Found by:** Felix noticing the grey dot on 7.d4, session e3bd1021-4d34-443f-96c0-a1af650f0984, 2026-10-01.
* **Handled, 2026-10-03:** The renderer's tree stores raw NAG codes (`TreeNode.nags: number[]`, 0–255, insertion order, duplicates kept) instead of 26 glyphs. One catalogue maps codes to glyphs (`$8` → □ and `$11` → = added), and one projection, `nagGlyphs`, feeds every display consumer, so a code without a glyph draws nothing and never displaces a known symbol. The PGN writer emits every code in ascending order, with a suffix glyph only for a first code of 1–6 (`[1, 2]` → `e4! $2`). Annotate toggles and `goToAnnotation` work on glyph classes. Tabs persisted in the old shape migrate in place without a version bump; invalid, corrupt or over-long legacy arrays keep the unreadable path. Known limit: a tab opened before the fix already lost `$8`/`$11` (and collapsed aliases such as `$23` → `$22`), so such tabs must be reopened from their file before saving. Decisions `d-20261003-15` through `d-20261003-19`. Commits `a6348c79` (implementation), `2f4dc8c4`, `3de938da`, `db20b0ec`, `fb69f852` (diff-review repairs and verify:app staging record). Real window: `pnpm verify:app` NAG scenario green, each of its nine assertions staged red. Display follow-up: `f-20261003-03`. Review: `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-01-lossless-nags-review.md`.

### The persisted `database-view` store hydrates `database` without validation, so a malformed stored handle crashes the database view instead of falling back to the overview

* **ID:** f-20261001-13 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/state/store/database.ts` (`persist` options `name: "database-view"`, `storage: createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)`, ~201-204: no `version`, `migrate` or `merge`); consumers `src/components/databases/databaseRoute.ts` (`sameDatabaseHandle(database.file, active?.file)`), `src/utils/pathCapabilities.ts` (`capabilityKey`, `pathRefKey`: `handle.id` dereference).
* **Defect:** read on HEAD `62c627b8`: the persist middleware restores `state.database` exactly as JSON-parsed. A stored `database` that is JSON-valid but not a `SuccessDatabaseInfo` (e.g. `{}` or `{ "file": {} }`, an older shape, or a hand-edited entry) reaches `capabilityKey(undefined)` / `pathRefKey(undefined)` and throws `TypeError` while rendering `DatabaseView` (via `resolveDatabaseRoute` → `sameDatabaseHandle` → `databaseHandleKey`). Whether WebKitGTK's sessionStorage survives an app restart (which would make an upgrade-time shape change reachable) was not measured.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` — "Persist only versioned, schema-validated user state and reconcile it against native state at startup." One bad entry turns the database page into a render crash rather than the overview.
* **Change:** validate the hydrated `database` at the store boundary (persist `merge`/`migrate` with a shape check of `type === "success"` and a handle whose key is a non-empty string; drop it otherwise), so every consumer can trust it; prove with a test that seeds `sessionStorage["database-view"]` with a malformed `database` and asserts the store hydrates with `database: undefined`.
* **Context:** surfaced by the `review-persisted-state` lens on the 2026-10-01 database Back-button plan (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-database-back-button.md`, issue R1-I1). That plan keeps its own sidebar resume link from widening the crash to every page; the pre-existing view/route crash is this finding.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, database Back-button plan review, 2026-10-01.
* **Cumulative implementation review, round D1 (2026-10-14):** The persisted-state lens found a remaining hydration failure at this store boundary. JSON-valid state with a valid selected database and games: {} restores an undefined query, the ready route does not reset it, and GameTable dereferences query.sides. The same worker must validate the restored active tab and complete nested panel/query state against actual consumer invariants, preserve valid panels and live actions, and use existing defaults for malformed panels. The selection-only schema does not complete this finding.

### A failed engine termination drops the actor from the supervisor, so no later owner can retry or confirm cleanup

* **ID:** f-20261001-14 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** engine-uci · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/engine/process.rs:1448-1461` (`terminate_exact`: `let result = current.actor.terminate().await; self.actors.remove(key); result`), used by `retire_engine`, `retire_executables`, `kill_engine`, `kill_engines` and tab termination.
* **Defect:** when `actor.terminate()` returns an error, the actor is removed from the registry anyway. The child process may still be alive (kill-on-drop is best effort), and nothing — tab close, app shutdown via `RunEvent::ExitRequested`, a later retirement — can find it again.
* **Why it matters:** `.claude/rules/async-resource-invariants.md` requires cleanup on every exit path; an engine with a large hash (8 GB in Felix's configuration) can outlive its owner unseen.
* **Open question:** keep failed actors in a bounded "reaping" set that shutdown and later retirements retry, or make termination escalate (kill, wait with deadline) until it is confirmed before removal — and how the renderer learns that a process could not be confirmed dead.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-engine-protocol` lens, round 2 of the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan review (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md`, issue R2 retirement-failure), confirmed by the orchestrator from source, 2026-10-01.
* **Additional review evidence (2026-10-09):** f-20260926-07 cumulative review traced the normally joined production game loop. src-tauri/src/game.rs logs a terminate_game_engines failure at the loop tail and returns (). Shared pending teardown subsequently removes the failed generation, so finish_retired's unconditional exact termination finds no registered or pending owner and returns Ok. This can make replacement and shutdown_all report success after an unconfirmed reap. Existing clean-join failure tests use a loop that skips engine cleanup and do not exercise that production loss path. The cause is this finding's failed-actor/result retention contract, not an empty-join cancellation gap. Preserve the completed outcome or failed generation until the owning game/shutdown path has observed failure. Verification for this finding must include the production-loop cleanup path, not only direct fallback teardown. The separate design question remains open at build tier. review-error-handling confidence 95, adopting drain a51461c5-317b-40c0-8297-ab16a2fc6904.

* **Cumulative implementation review, round D1 (2026-10-14):** Correctness, root-cause and engine-protocol lenses independently found that terminate_observed captures the actor before the per-key lifecycle wait but attaches to PendingTermination only afterward. A concurrent exact terminator can therefore start a successful retry after the original attempt failed and lose the failure it overlapped. Correctness also found that concurrent LiveSession retirement can see an empty join slot while another owner still awaits it, then treat an unset loop outcome as success and release capacity prematurely. Both violate the adopted O2/O4 consumer promises and remain Fix obligations of this anchor. Tests and minimalism found the test-only TASK_JOIN_DIAGNOSTICS vector duplicates the logger rather than proving actual log emission. Other accepted repairs strengthen production-loop retained error assertions, share quit/write-line logic, name capacity for unobserved sessions and correct child ownership documentation. No claim of completed review or release is made.

### Engine archive staging reopens the destination parent by pathname

* **ID:** f-20261001-15 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/fs.rs:1319-1329` (`download_engine_archive_core`: `destination_parent = resolved.target().parent().to_path_buf()`, then `private_tempdir_in(".archive", &destination_parent)`).
* **Defect:** the staging directory is created under a pathname derived from the resolved destination rather than through the verified directory descriptor. If the engine root is renamed and its path replaced by a symlink between resolution and `private_tempdir_in`, download and extraction write staging data under the symlink target; the later atomic install refuses publication, but only after those out-of-authority writes happened.
* **Why it matters:** every other path-authority write door binds to a verified inode; this one is a pathname re-open in the same class the path-authority work closed elsewhere. Reaching it needs a local actor racing the rename, so it is outside accidental-input threat models.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-tauri-security` lens, round 2 of the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan review, 2026-10-01; confirmed by the orchestrator reading `fs.rs:1319-1329`.
* **Why rejected:** Reopen-by-path matters only against a same-user local attacker who already owns the user's files; never observed. Not worth fixing under universal rule 4d (only a defect with a cost is a finding; setup cleanup 2026-10-13).

## 2026-10-01 — filed through the inbox spool

### A `.tar.gz` engine archive is only gunzipped, never untarred, so no Linux or macOS catalog Stockfish can install

* **ID:** f-20261001-16 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/fs.rs:589-640` (format detection from the first 512 bytes: zip magic, gzip magic, or raw `ustar`), `src-tauri/src/fs.rs:1681-1710` (`extract_gz_cancellable` decompresses into one file via `atomic_replace`), `src/utils/engines.ts:323-331` (`installDefaultEngine` then registers the manifest's nested `path`), `src/catalogs/engines.json` (Stockfish 19 linux and macOS entries are `.tar.gz`).
* **Defect:** a gzip payload is classified as `is_gz` before any tar check, and the decompressed stream is written as a single file. The tar members (`stockfish/stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal` and siblings) are never extracted, so `registerInstalledEngine(root, "stockfish/stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal")` cannot find the executable. Only zip assets (Windows Stockfish, RubiChess, Lc0) can reach registration.
* **Why it matters:** the default-engine catalog's flagship entry cannot be installed on Linux or macOS; together with `f-20261001-06` the catalog install path is unusable on those platforms.
* **Fix shape:** detect a tar stream inside the gzip (ustar magic at offset 257 of the decompressed head) and extract it through `extract_tar_cancellable` with the same entry, ratio and expanded-size limits; plain `.gz` single files keep today's path. Prove with a gzip-of-tar fixture through the download-install core and a registration of the nested path, red on today's code.
* **Planned:** obligation O2 of `tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-plan` lens, round 2 of the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan review, confirmed by the orchestrator reading `fs.rs:589-640,1681-1710`, 2026-10-01.

Handled by `f19e14ac` (Stockfish 19 upgrade build, phase P2, obligation O2). A gzip whose decompressed head carries the ustar magic is extracted through `extract_tar_cancellable`, with the whole decompressed stream bounded by the expanded-size and compression-ratio limits; a plain single-file `.gz` keeps its path. Red-first Rust tests: gzip-of-tar install plus nested registration, and ratio and expanded-size rejections. Real proof: `fs::tests::real_stockfish19_catalog_install_answers_uci` (ignored, network) installed the signed SF19 Linux artefact into `stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal.tar.gz-<full sha256>/`, registered `stockfish/stockfish-linux-x86-64-universal`, and the binary answered `id name Stockfish 19` / `uciok` with exit 0.

### `enginesAtom` publishes a new engine list before its owner save resolves, so a refused save leaves memory ahead of storage

* **ID:** f-20261001-17 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/state/atoms.ts:244-260` (`set(storedEnginesAtom, next)` publishes in memory first), `src/state/engineOwnerStorage.ts:166-228` (receipt `saved:false` without restoring), callers `src/components/engines/EnginesPage.tsx:385-397` (settings edits), `:649-662` (Duplicate selects `selected + 1` immediately), `:676-683` (Remove retires the id before the save, per `d-20260901-17`).
* **Defect:** after a refused save (attachment prepare failure, quota, invalid record) the in-memory list keeps the unsaved value for the rest of the session while storage holds the old one. The refusal is notified (`reportPersistError` → `notifyListenerError`), but the UI keeps showing and using state that will vanish on restart.
* **Why it matters:** violates the persisted-state write/read symmetry the rules ask for; the user acts on a list that is not durable.
* **Open question:** a general fix interacts with three callers: restoring the old value after refusal makes Remove (which retires the id first, `d-20260901-17`) leave a visible but tombstoned engine and makes Duplicate's immediate selection index a missing entry; publishing only after the save makes per-keystroke settings edits wait on an IPC round trip. Which contract — optimistic with restore plus reordered Remove/Duplicate, or staged publication with a local draft for edits — and does it supersede `d-20260901-17`'s ordering?
* **Context:** the Stockfish 19 upgrade plan (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-stockfish-19-upgrade.md`) gives catalog install and upgrade a publish-after-save path of their own; this finding covers every other caller.
* **Found by:** Codex lenses `review-correctness`, `review-persisted-state`, `review-error-handling`, `review-plan` (rounds 1-2 of that plan review), confirmed by the orchestrator from source, 2026-10-01.
* **Handled 2026-10-15:** Ordinary enginesAtom candidates publish only after saved:true, with responsive identity-guarded field/option drafts and current-record merges. One analysis action saves one candidate and receipt. Duplicate, add, JSON and form completion use receipts, selection ownership and current identities. Local removeLocalId alone publishes omission before save and keeps it on refusal, then existing retirement cleanup runs, under d-20261007-10 and d-20261014-25/26/27. No generic optimistic writer or second persistence queue was introduced. Engine source ac464d4c and repairs6a6d1e99/e6f8257b. Real-store owner/caller/listener proofs include389 targeted and1919 importer tests, TypeScript and pre-review/contract. Source-only old publication causes actual native EP2-card/EP2-input failures1 and restores0. Six native assertions each have distinctive staged failure messages at actual exit1, exact input/method restoration and ordinary recovery0. Final product browser48cases and fresh native proof0 cover current source. Rejected ordinary optimistic publication/rollback and a generic after-save opt-in, preserved the restricted removal contract. Co-located font validation is handled separately, puzzle ownership design remains its own build. Verified current source commit b7f4511de05950f2f72bfbdb1fe65caa5e6ea60b. Full tracked evidence and honest transport/picker limits: tasks/handoffs/2026-10-15-f-20261001-17-review.md. Final clean-tree gates and push follow closure review. ### The persisted reference database handle is searched even when that database is no longer readable

* **ID:** f-20261001-18 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** inline · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/panels/database/DatabasePanel.tsx` (~161-165: `setLocalOptions((q) => ({ ...q, path: referenceDatabase }))` copies the persisted handle into the local search options; `fetchOpening` ~120-126 then calls `searchPosition` with it), `src/state/atoms.ts` (~457-460: `referenceDbAtom` persisted in localStorage).
* **Defect:** the dropdown narrows to `type === "success"` entries, but the persisted `referenceDbAtom` handle is never checked against the current database list. A reference database that later becomes unreadable (uninitialised after a failed import, corrupt, deleted outside the app) is still queried by the local explorer, which then fails on every position instead of showing "no reference database".
* **Fix shape:** resolve the persisted handle against the current `getDatabases` result; treat a missing or error entry as no selection (and say so in the panel) without silently clearing the user's stored choice on a transient list failure.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-correctness` and `review-plan` lenses, round 2 of the plan review for the PGN long-comment import fix (`tasks/plans/2026-10-01-pgn-long-comment-import.md`, issue P13), 2026-10-01. Pre-existing; identical before that plan (the entry was dropped from the list, the handle stayed persisted).
* **Implemented, 2026-10-25:** Commit 72caa66a derives one effective local-explorer reference from successful current database-list entries. Missing, unreadable, pending and failed-list states cannot start a stale search. The picker, synchronous search path and all three panel warnings agree, while the persisted reference, option filters, collection retargeting and online explorer remain intact. Existing NoDatabaseWarning is reused, with no new UI text or native contract.
* **Proof:** All 17 focused component tests pass. Restoring only the original production component through Git, with all new tests retained, produces eight expected failures, including stale queries against absent and unreadable handles. Restoring the fix passes all 17 again. The canonical container browser journey proves no search while unreadable, preserved storage and resumed search after Library revalidation. All 30 affected database-files journeys pass with no snapshot changes. Root inspected the final runtime PNG. ### A running local PGN import cannot be cancelled from the UI

* **ID:** f-20261001-19 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** pgn-import · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` (~222-244: the "Convert: …" progress line has no cancel control), `src/components/databases/AddDatabase.tsx` (`convertLocalDatabase`), `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` (`convert_pgn`, ~727-786: no ticket parameter; only application shutdown cancels it through `state.operations`), also "Add games" (`DatabasesPage.tsx` ~471-498, `databaseMutation.ts` ~57-75).
* **Defect:** importing a reference database (Mega Database 2025: 11.4 M games, ~10 min) blocks the "+" button and the Databases page for the whole run with no way to stop it short of quitting the app. Downloadable databases in the same modal already offer cancel (`cancelDownloadJob`, `AddDatabase.tsx` ~318). The backend already rolls a cancelled import back as one unit (`f-20260912-04`).
* **Fix shape:** give `convert_pgn` a cancellation ticket like the download jobs, add a cancel control to the progress line, and make the renderer flow delete the freshly created database on cancel (the cleanup path the long-comment import fix adds for failures).
* **Open question:** does cancel reuse the download-job ticket registry (`cancelDownloadJob`) or get its own operation ticket, and does a cancelled import of a *new* database delete the file in the backend or in the renderer flow that created it.
* **Why `build`:** IPC contract change (new ticket parameter, regenerated bindings) plus renderer UI.
* **Found by:** Claude, session 617a946f, 2026-10-01, while diagnosing Felix's vanished Mega Database import.
* **Correction (2026-10-01, records review):** the Defect sentence overstates the blocking. During a local conversion only "Add New" and local-conversion submission are disabled and the target database is hidden from the list (`DatabasesPage.tsx` ~86 and ~225, `AddDatabase.tsx` ~168); the rest of the Databases page stays usable and the add modal can be closed while the import continues. What is missing is unchanged: there is no control that stops the running import short of quitting the app.

## 2026-10-01 — filed through the inbox spool

### Database storage size is declared `bigint` but crosses IPC as a JSON number

* **ID:** f-20261001-20 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** bindings-ipc · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/bindings/generated.ts:1135` (`DatabaseInfo.storage_size: bigint`), its Rust source field in `src-tauri/src/db/**`, `src/state/store/database.ts:201-204` (the persisted `database-view` store that serializes a `SuccessDatabaseInfo` with `JSON.stringify`), and test fixtures that cast around it (`src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx`, `src/components/databases/ConcurrentConversion.test.tsx`: `storage_size: 1 as unknown as bigint`).
* **Defect:** Specta declares the Rust `u64` storage size as `bigint`, but Tauri serializes it as a JSON number, so every runtime `DatabaseInfo` carries a number while the type says `bigint`. A value that really is a `bigint` (as the declared type invites, e.g. a fixture `1n`) makes the persisted `database-view` store throw `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt` on `setDatabase`. The tests of the database Back fix (2026-10-01) had to cast `1 as unknown as bigint` to store a database at all. Same class as `f-20260925-02` (progress generations) for a different field; `src/utils/db.ts` already documents it once for the downloadable catalog ("JSON cannot represent the native bigint storage size").
* **Evidence:** In the Back-fix phase, the write leaf changed the `ConcurrentConversion.test.tsx` fixture from `storage_size: 1n` to a number cast once that suite started calling `activeDatabaseViewStore.getState().setDatabase(...)`. The store persists through `createJSONStorage(() => sessionStorage)`. No runtime defect is observed today because production values are numbers.
* **Open question:** Should the binding declare the wire type honestly (a Specta type override to `number`, with a documented 2^53 bound for byte counts), or should the renderer normalize at the `getDatabases` facade? Decide together with `f-20260925-02` so `u64` fields follow one rule.
* **Scope:** `DatabaseInfo.storage_size` and any other `u64` field of `DatabaseInfo`; no change to the persisted store schema beyond what the type fix requires.
* **Related:** `f-20260925-02` (same `u64` → `bigint` wire mismatch, progress generations); no shared Root assigned until the two are decided together.
* **Proof sought:** A fixture built from the generated type with no cast can be stored in `activeDatabaseViewStore` and round-trips through sessionStorage; `pnpm bindings:check` stays green.
* **Correction (2026-10-01, push review):** the **Where** line overstates one detail: `src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx` casts `storage_size: 0 as unknown as bigint`, and `src/components/databases/ConcurrentConversion.test.tsx` casts `1 as unknown as bigint`. Both are the same `as unknown as bigint` workaround; the finding is otherwise unchanged.

## 2026-10-01 — filed through the inbox spool

### Two conversions into the same database share one progress id, so one import's progress can show as the other's

* **ID:** f-20261001-21 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** pgn-import · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/utils/db.ts` (~117-118, `conversionProgressId(handle)` derives the id from the database handle alone), `src/hooks/useConversionProgress.ts` (~35-45 accepts any `ConvertProgress` whose id matches the target handle), callers `src/components/home/AccountCard.tsx` (account sync) and `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` "Add games" (`databaseMutation.ts`); Rust emits the caller's id unchanged (`src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` `convert_pgn_blocking`).
* **Defect:** if "Add games" is still converting into a database when account sync starts a conversion into the same database (or the reverse), both send the same progress id. The conversion line then shows whichever frame arrived last: the other import's game count, elapsed time or source file name. Rule `async-resource-invariants.md`: "Assume a response belongs to the most recent request because it arrived last — use a discriminator, never timing."
* **Fix shape:** make the progress id per conversion (handle + a per-call nonce minted by the caller), carried through the existing `progressId` parameter; the renderer owner state stores the full id, not only the handle. No IPC signature change is needed.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-ipc-contract` lens over the cumulative diff of the PGN long-comment import fix, 2026-10-01 (pre-existing; not introduced by that diff).
* **Closed (already fixed, verified 2026-10-13):** the defect no longer exists at HEAD. Commit `9566f68a` (f-20260914-06, 2026-10-04, "track each PGN conversion by its own operation id") removed `conversionProgressId(handle)`: every conversion now mints `conversion:<uuid>` in `runDatabaseConversion` (`src/state/atoms.ts`) before any IPC call, and `useConversionProgress` applies a frame only to the entry carrying that id and never creates one. Two "Add games" runs into the same database therefore carry independent ids; `src/components/databases/ConcurrentConversion.test.tsx` ("two Add games runs into the same target retain independent ids, frames and rows") pins it. Verified by reading `src/state/atoms.ts:506-551` and `src/hooks/useConversionProgress.ts` at `e96de980` during the f-20261001-11 Library build (session fab6795c-3780-4adc-8356-6d9441cd768f), whose extraction kept the same `runDatabaseConversion` path. No code change in this session.

### Database deletion, including its new -wal/-shm cleanup, has no Windows runtime test

* **ID:** f-20261001-22 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` — the database test module is gated `#[cfg(all(test, unix))]` (~3656), so `delete_database_blocking` / `unlink_database_files` tests (including `zero_table_delete_removes_database_and_sqlite_sidecars`, added 2026-10-01) never run on the Windows CI target.
* **Defect:** deletion of a database and its sidecars (search index, legacy index, SQLite `-wal`/`-shm`) relies on identity probes and unlink semantics that differ on Windows (open handles, sharing modes, delete-pending). Windows CI compiles this code but executes none of its tests, so a Windows-only failure to remove a sidecar, or a sharing violation from a still-open pool connection, would pass every gate.
* **Fix shape:** move the platform-independent deletion tests into a module that also runs on Windows (fixtures without unix-only helpers), or add Windows-specific variants; run them in the existing `rust-windows-test` lane.
* **Related:** `f-20260914-08` (workspace delete refused on Windows, handled) carries the earlier Windows deletion decisions.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-platform-semantics` lens over the cumulative diff of the PGN long-comment import fix, 2026-10-01 (pre-existing gating).
* **Handled (2026-10-02, Claude Code drain 837e01c1, lens tier):** the database deletion tests now run on every target. `46950c4b` moved the 22 deletion tests that need no unix-only machinery from the `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` into a new `#[cfg(test)] mod deletion_tests` in `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs`: the four `finish_database_deletion_*` cases, every `unlink_database_files_*` case, the legacy and colliding sidecar cases, `zero_table_delete_removes_database_and_sqlite_sidecars`, both sidecar-failure variants (with registry-cleanup failure), the symlinked `-wal`/`-shm` refusal (now through a per-platform `symlink_file` helper), and the malformed-revision, busy, directory-substitution and legacy-revision-1 delete cases. The fixtures they share with the unix module (`blocking_database_case`, `arbitrary_database_case`, `seed_search_cache_for_database`, `install_atomic_export_failure` with its injector types) were hoisted once to module-level `cfg(test)` items, and `CREATE_TABLES_SQL`, `schema_database_case`, `set_unlink_sidecar_after_identity_probe_hook` and the `test_target` re-export were relaxed from `all(test, unix)` to `test`. `7f1488f9` (review round 1 repair) renamed the misnamed substitution test to `unlink_database_files_preserves_sqlite_sidecars_after_primary_substitution` and moved the platform-independent source-scan test into `deletion_tests`.
* **Proof:** Linux `cargo test --bins -- db::deletion_tests` gives 23 passed. CI run 36956003834 on `7f1488f9`: `rust-windows-test` succeeded, and its log shows all 23 `db::deletion_tests::*` passing on windows-latest (933 passed, 0 failed). `rust-macos-test` and every `rust-platform` target also succeeded. Local `pnpm gates:push -- --rust` passed on rerun.
* **Left unix-only, on purpose:** the tests that drive the removal fault injector (`crate::infra::fs::unix::inject_removal` exists only in the unix removal path) and `legacy_sidecar_read_permission_failure_propagates` (unix permission bits). `symlinked_ancestor_database_indexes_and_deletes_through_its_real_directory` also stays unix-only, because its substance is Windows path-authority ancestor resolution rather than deletion; it was filed through the inbox from this run.
* **Rejected:** ungating the whole 8,000-line `mod tests`. That would be a port of every database test, each needing its own Windows triage, and goes well beyond this finding. Also rejected: duplicating the fixtures into the new module (rule 11).
* **Also filed from this run:** the first final-gate run's coverage lane failed once on `db::repository::tests::lru_evicts_the_least_recently_used_idle_entry` with `Conflict("database is open through another directory")`. The process-global binding registry collides on an inode that a parallel test frees and another test reuses. The rerun was green, and the flake was filed through the inbox at `build` tier.

## 2026-10-01 — filed through the inbox spool

### "Add games" overwrites the single shared conversion state, so a running local import loses its progress line and its guards

* **ID:** f-20261001-23 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/state/atoms.ts` (~488-500: `databaseConversionStateAtom` is one slot; `clearOwnedConversion(handle)` resets it when `targetDatabase` matches), `src/components/databases/DatabasesPage.tsx` (~494-503: "Add games" sets `targetDatabase: dest` over whatever conversion is running and clears it with `clearOwnedConversion(dest)` when it finishes), `src/components/databases/AddDatabase.tsx` (local conversion owns the same slot).
* **Defect:** if "Add games" starts while a local PGN import is still converting, it replaces the slot's owner with its own target. When it finishes first, its cleanup resets the slot to idle while the local import is still running: the "Convert: …" progress line disappears and "Add New" plus local-conversion submission are enabled again, so a second import can start beside the first. The local import's own `clearOwnedConversion` later finds a different owner and does nothing. Distinct from `f-20261001-21` (same-database progress-id collision): this is two different databases sharing one state slot.
* **Fix shape:** key conversion state by owner (a map of running conversions, or refuse to start a second conversion while one is running); the progress line and the guards read "any conversion running".
* **Found by:** Codex records lens, closure round d3 of the PGN long-comment import fix, 2026-10-01 (pre-existing).
* **Closed (already fixed, verified 2026-10-13):** the single shared slot no longer exists. Commit `9566f68a` (f-20260914-06, 2026-10-04) turned `databaseConversionStateAtom` into an ordered `DatabaseConversionEntry[]` registry; `runDatabaseConversion` adds one entry per operation and removes only its own id on every exit path, and `clearOwnedConversion` is gone. The progress rows render one per entry and "Add new"/local conversion gating reads "any conversion running" (`conversionState.length > 0`). Pinned by `src/components/databases/ConcurrentConversion.test.tsx` ("$route $outcome removes only its own entry beside Add games"). Verified at `e96de980` in the f-20261001-11 Library build (session fab6795c-3780-4adc-8356-6d9441cd768f): the extracted `src/components/databases/useDatabaseLibrary.tsx` keeps that registry and gating unchanged. No code change in this session.

### The symlinked-ancestor database index-and-delete test never runs on Windows

* **ID:** f-20261002-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** non-linux-platform-port · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 837e01c1-7c21-4f1a-83e3-7e56d2b8a9d1

* **Defect:** the test grants a database through a symlinked parent directory, builds and loads its search index, and deletes the database and its index sidecar through the real directory. None of that runs in `rust-windows-test`, so a Windows-only failure of a directory-symlink (or junction) ancestor in grant, promotion, canonical resolution, index generation or deletion passes every gate. The f-20261001-22 slice moved the 22 deletion tests that need no unix-only machinery into the cross-platform `mod deletion_tests`; this one was left because its substance is Windows path-authority ancestor resolution (`f-20260914-33`, `f-20260914-36` settled the unix-side spelling), not deletion.
* **Fix shape:** a per-platform directory-symlink helper (`std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir` on Windows; the CI runner can create symlinks, precedent `windows_reparse_sidecar_is_reported_as_present_but_never_followed` in `db/repository.rs`), move the test into `mod deletion_tests` or a Windows variant beside it, and decide from the Windows path-authority code whether a symlinked ancestor must be accepted or refused there — then assert that.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-platform-semantics` lens over the f-20261001-22 diff, 2026-10-02.
* **Handled (2026-10-02, Claude Code drain 83be2012, lens tier):** the linked-ancestor database test now runs on every target. `0487a998` moved `symlinked_ancestor_database_indexes_and_deletes_through_its_real_directory` out of the unix-only `mod tests` into the cross-platform `mod deletion_tests` as `assert_linked_ancestor_database_indexes_and_deletes(link_directory)`. It is driven by a per-platform directory symlink on every target and, on Windows only, by a directory junction (`junction_ancestor_database_indexes_and_deletes_through_its_real_directory`). The four copies of the `cmd /C mklink /J` fixture became one `#[cfg(all(test, windows))]` helper, `infra::fs::windows_test_junction`, and every Windows junction test routes through it. Push-review repairs: `490074f7` merged `symlink_file`/`symlink_dir` into one `symlink(target, link, target_is_dir)` helper. `ab027a3d` extracted `PathAuthority::grant_persistent_file_for_test`, `database_app_with_grant` and `full_database_operations`, and routed all seven grant-then-promote fixture copies in `db/mod.rs` through them.
* **Accept or refuse on Windows — settled by `d-20260915-03`, not re-derived:** accept. The `#[cfg(windows)]` arm of `acquire_target` (`infra/path_authority/mod.rs`) canonicalises the parent through `canonical_binding` and then proves the canonical spelling no-follow with `open_verified_parent`, the same as the unix arm. ### Parallel tests can collide in the process-global SQLite binding registry through a reused inode

* **ID:** f-20261002-02 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 837e01c1-7c21-4f1a-83e3-7e56d2b8a9d1
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/bound_sqlite.rs` (~175-200: `REGISTRY` is process-global, and `BoundDatabase::acquire` refuses with `Conflict("database is open through another directory")` when any live binding has the same `(dev, ino)` identity under a different parent, `d-20260929-05`); `src-tauri/src/db/repository.rs` (~2712 `lru_evicts_the_least_recently_used_idle_entry`, the observed victim).
* **Defect:** the `pnpm gates:push -- --rust` coverage lane on `7f1488f9` (2026-10-02, f-20261001-22 drain release) failed once with `db::repository::tests::lru_evicts_the_least_recently_used_idle_entry` panicking at `repository.rs:2722` on `Conflict("database is open through another directory")`; the plain `rust-test` lane of the same run, and the rerun of all lanes, passed. All unit tests share one process and therefore one binding registry. If any test keeps a binding alive after its database file is unlinked (tempdir dropped, test-owned deletion), the freed inode can be reused by another test's new database in a different tempdir, and that test's acquire is refused. Which test outlives its file with a live binding is not yet determined. Commit `46950c4b` moved 22 database deletion tests into `db::deletion_tests`, which changes the test name ordering and so the interleaving; it did not add any binding holder.
* **Open question:** is the fix test-side isolation (per-test registry scope, or tests guaranteeing every binding is dropped before their file is removed) or a product-side refinement of the identity key (e.g. also refusing only while the leaf inode is still linked), given that in the product an inode cannot be reused while a SQLite connection holds the leaf open?
* **Fix shape:** first find the binding holder that outlives its file (instrument `Registry` in tests to report bindings whose leaf no longer exists at test end), then decide the question above; a reproduction can force inode reuse by creating and deleting files in a loop on the same filesystem.
* **Found by:** Claude Code drain session 837e01c1-7c21-4f1a-83e3-7e56d2b8a9d1 (next-finding f-20261001-22), final push gate, 2026-10-02. Gate log: `artifacts/gates/20261002T022755619Z-3234038/rust-coverage.log`.
* **Recurrence 2026-10-02 (Stockfish 19 build run, final gates on `d1b301e2`):** the `backend-test` lane of `pnpm gates:push -- --rust --frontend --bindings` failed with a third victim, `db::repository::tests::lru_never_evicts_an_active_lease` (panic at `repository.rs:2702`, same `Conflict("database is open through another directory")`); 1716 passed, 1 failed. The run's diff touches nothing under `src-tauri/src/db/`. Three distinct victim tests now share the mechanism, so the fix belongs in the registry/test isolation, not in any one test.

Every victim passes alone. The new admission doors (capability opens and SQLite sidecar opens, `src-tauri/src/infra/inode_ownership.rs` `check_class`) consult the same `(dev, ino)` registry, so the flake now also surfaces as `Conflict("file is open through a SQLite binding")` and as a refused sidecar open (`unable to open database file`). It now needs fixing ahead of its age, because remote CI runs the same suite.
* **Mechanism observed while tracing (not yet a decision):** of the registry's owners, only a published primary `Registration` (`src-tauri/src/db/bound_sqlite.rs`, `Binding` keeps a parent `File` and a leaf name) holds no descriptor of its own inode; capability owners, sidecar pins and quarantine entries all hold one, so their inode cannot be recycled while registered. A candidate product-side fix is to pin each registration's leaf inode for the registration's lifetime — Linux an `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW` descriptor (closing it releases no POSIX lock, the property `d-20260930-10` already relies on); other Unix an ordinary descriptor that closes only in `Registration::drop`, after every connection of that registration has closed and so while this process holds no SQLite lock on the inode — verified against the key's identity at creation. Then `(dev, ino)` cannot be reused while any entry names it, in tests and in the product (an idle cached binding of an externally deleted file would keep its inode until eviction). The trade-off against test-side isolation is still this finding's open question.

* **ID:** f-20261002-03 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** inline · **Blocked:** none

* **Defect:** each site spells out the two-step `grant_dialog_operations(path, name, PathClass::BoundedDialogGrant, operations.clone(), <ttl>, <uses>)` then `promote_dialog(&grant, <persistent class>, name, operations)` sequence by hand. Production callers (`main.rs` dialog commands) are out of scope: they are the contract, not a fixture.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-minimalism` lens, push round 2 of the f-20261002-01 drain release, 2026-10-02.

## 2026-10-02 — filed through the inbox spool

### Superseded catalog engine install directories stay on disk forever once their handle is pruned

* **ID:** f-20261002-04 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs:6594` (startup pruning filters unowned registry entries), `:6623` (commits the pruned registry), `:8096` (the commit body saves registry state and deletes no file or tree); `src/utils/engines.ts` `installCatalogEngine` (each verified artefact installs into its own `<archive>-<full sha256>` directory under the engine workspace, commit `f19e14ac`).
* **Defect:** catalog installs are now version-unique and are never replaced (adoption, `D9`). After an upgrade (Stockfish 18 → 19, later 19 → 20) the old entry's handle becomes unowned and is pruned from the path registry at the next startup, but nothing ever removes the app-owned install directory it pointed at. The same holds for an install whose save was refused, and for an artefact downloaded and then discarded after a cancel intent.
* **Why it matters:** an unbounded retention: every catalog version installed stays on disk (the Stockfish 19 Linux tree alone is about 80 MB extracted plus its NNUE files), invisible in the UI. The async-resource rule requires every registry that holds a resource to have a bounded retention policy.
* **Open question:** which directories are safe to delete and when: only directories under the app-owned engine workspace that no registry entry references after pruning, and never while an engine child (including a running game that keeps its old binary until it ends, plan O3) may still be executing from them. Delete at startup after pruning, or on the next upgrade? Windows refuses to delete a running executable.
* **Measured:** the P2 write leaf of the Stockfish 19 upgrade read the pruning path (lines above) and found no tree deletion; the plan's "Risks / open questions" required this check and a filed finding rather than a reaper in that run.
* **Found by:** Stockfish 19 upgrade build, phase P2, 2026-10-02 (Codex leaf investigation, confirmed by the orchestrator's review of the cited lines' role).
* **Correction (2026-10-02, records lens):** the size claim above was not measured. Measured: the extracted Stockfish 19 Linux release tree (`stockfish/`, including sources, wiki and scripts that ship in the archive) is 101 MB (`du -sh`), from an 81 MB download. The Windows sentence is an expectation from plan `D9` (replacing a tree fails while its binary runs), not a measured deletion attempt.

* **ID:** f-20261002-05 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** native-fs · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/main.rs:2482` (the path registry is `app_config_dir()/path-authority.json`), `src-tauri/src/main.rs:1501-1525` (`get_engine_workspace_blocking`: `ensure_app_owned_default_dir(... Engines)` then `get_or_create_engine_root` + `set_active_engine_root`, which persist the registry), `src/utils/engines.ts` `installCatalogEngine` (first call is `tauri.getEngineWorkspace()`).
* **Defect:** on a profile where `~/.config/com.chessriddle.encroissant/` does not exist yet (a fresh install that has never persisted a path), `get_engine_workspace` creates `<app data>/engines` and then fails with `missing-resource` / "I/O failure: No such file or directory (os error 2)", because the registry write targets a config directory nobody created. Measured 2026-10-02 against the release build in a throwaway `HOME` driven through `scripts/app-driver.mjs`: invoking `get_engine_workspace` returned `{"tag":"backend-error","category":"missing-resource","message":"I/O failure"}` and the log line `native operation failed ... label=get_engine_workspace: I/O failure: No such file or directory (os error 2)`; with only `mkdir -p ~/.config/com.chessriddle.encroissant` added before launch, the same call returned an `engineRoot` handle.
* **Why it matters:** the Add Engine catalog card shows "Downloading" and silently returns to "Install" for a new user, and the new "Upgrade from catalog" action fails the same way; whichever native path write happens first on a new profile is exposed to the same missing parent. Existing profiles that already wrote the registry (Felix's) are unaffected.
* **Open question:** where the config directory is created and with which mode: once at startup next to `AppDataDir::for_app` (and whether that changes the registry's durability contract for a missing-versus-unreadable registry), or lazily inside the registry's atomic save. Check every other first write under `app_config_dir()` for the same gap.

* **Correction (2026-10-02, records lens):** "silently" is wrong. `AddEngine.tsx:230-233` passes the failure to `notifyUnlessCancelled`, so an error notification is raised; the measurement sampled the page text only every 20 s and missed the transient toast. ## 2026-10-02 — filed through the inbox spool

### A failed progress clear leaves a stale terminal record that every remounted progress bar shows again

* **ID:** f-20261002-07 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-state · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src/hooks/downloadJobs.ts:41-48` (`clearDownloadProgress` is best effort: on failure it logs and returns `null`), `:84-85` (the job owner's failure cleanup swallows that result), `src/components/common/ProgressButton.tsx:~65` (a failed cancel request returns before any fence), `src/hooks/useProgress.ts` (the fence is a per-hook-instance ref reset on every mount), `src-tauri/src/progress.rs` (the backend keeps the terminal record until a clear succeeds).
* **Defect:** when `clearProgress` fails after a job ended — a discarded catalog download whose cancel request also failed (Upgrade from catalog, CR-1 of the Stockfish 19 plan), or an Add Engine install whose configuration probe failed after the download completed (pre-existing, already at `1a8ee277`: `src/utils/engines.ts:326-331` → the same cleanup) — the backend keeps the succeeded record. The hook that was showing it may fence it, but any remount (reopening the dialog) reads it again through `getProgress` and shows a retained 100 % bar beside the action until the app restarts.
* **Why it matters:** a bar that claims a finished download for something that was discarded or failed; it is cosmetic in effect (`CatalogEngineCard.tsx:53` keeps the completed label tied to native success), but it is state the user cannot clear.
* **Open question:** who owns the cleanup guarantee: the backend (a discarded or failed job never stays "succeeded", e.g. the job owner reports the outcome and the backend clears or marks it), the job owner (retry the clear with backoff before releasing the job), or the renderer (a fence that survives remounts, with a global bound). A renderer-only fence map was tried in the Stockfish 19 build (`cd8c72c5`) and withdrawn by a focused `review-plan` judgment: it added global mutable state for a pre-existing hazard and still missed the path where the cancel request itself failed.
* **Found by:** Stockfish 19 upgrade build, cumulative review closure rounds 6-7 (`review-error-handling`, CR-1 residual) and the focused `review-plan` judgment, 2026-10-02.
* **Correction (2026-10-02, records lens and round-8 lenses of the Stockfish 19 upgrade push, verified by the orchestrator in `src-tauri/src/progress.rs:14-16,99-103,221-231`):** the backend does not keep a terminal record until a clear succeeds. Terminal records expire after `TERMINAL_TTL` = 5 minutes and are purged on every read; capacity eviction (1 000 entries) can remove them sooner; and starting a job with the same progress id replaces the entry. So the stale bar shows on a remount for at most five minutes after the failed clear, or until the action is started again — not "every remount … until the app restarts", and the user can clear it by retrying. One failed clear suffices; the cancel request need not also fail (a cancel whose native work already finished returns `Ok(false)`; a route unmount records intent without sending a cancel).

### Search-index identity uses Path::exists, which treats a preferred-sidecar stat error as absence

* **ID:** f-20261002-12 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** db-search · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/main.rs:185-199` (`SearchIndexIdentity::for_database`: `preferred_index.exists()` then `legacy.exists()`), called from `src-tauri/src/db/search.rs:360` (`cache_loaded_index`) after `open_valid_preferred` has already opened the preferred sidecar (`src-tauri/src/db/search.rs:214-222`).
* **Defect:** `Path::exists` returns false when metadata cannot be read. Measured 2026-10-02 on this machine: a file inside a mode-0 directory gives `exists=Ok(false)` and `try_exists=Err(PermissionDenied)` (os error 13). If that check fails while the legacy sidecar is accessible, `for_database` selects the legacy path and returns `Ok`. The caller has already opened the preferred mmap, so the preferred bytes can be cached under the legacy identity. This is the behavior today. Moving the same calls into `infra/fs.rs` under the `f-20260912-03` plan does not change it.
* **Open question:** when the preferred sidecar's metadata cannot be read, should `for_database` return that I/O error, or keep treating an unverifiable preferred path as absent and fall through to the legacy sidecar?
* **Why it matters:** a permission or stat failure can publish the already-opened preferred index under the legacy cache key instead of failing the load.
* **Proof:** there is no failing command today, because this is the current `Path::exists` result. After a decision, the anchor is a unix test that places the preferred sidecar in a mode-0 directory, leaves the legacy sidecar readable, and asserts either `Err(PermissionDenied)` or the legacy identity, matching that decision.
* **Related:** `f-20260912-07` (handled; Root `sqlite-pathname-open`; the loader trusts a sidecar validated against an earlier probe — a different TOCTOU, not this stat-error fallback), `f-20260912-03` (the gate-scripts plan that moves these `exists` calls unchanged and files this question instead of changing the failure semantic).
* **Found by:** Codex `review-error-handling` during plan review of `tasks/plans/2026-10-02-pathname-method-surface.md` for `f-20260912-03`, 2026-10-02.
* **Handled (2026-10-08, Codex drain):** Implementation `9247edf2` removes the six production pathname reaches, every statement-level disallowed-method expectation, and both R5 baseline entries. SearchIndexIdentity stamps the exact opened preferred-sidecar descriptor and carries the authority target's database binding. Invalidation takes DatabaseFileTarget and evicts by matching database path or object. Stamp errors propagate without legacy fallback or cache publication. The database probe remains the linearization point and cancellation/invalidation still control publication.
* **Proof:** Root independently ran cargo fmt, Linux all-target clippy, `pnpm rust:windows:check`, unfiltered `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin chessfable` (2,079 passed, two ignored), all 298 release-surface checker tests, `pnpm gates:contract:check`, the disallowed-method grep (only crate-root test allowance), and `pnpm checks:pre-review`. Five documented Git-derived or selective-withdrawal witnesses failed at the intended runtime assertions and passed after byte-for-byte restoration. Windows and macOS runtime evidence is required from pushed-head CI before this run completes.
* **Decisions and limits:** d-20261008-15, d-20261008-16 and d-20261008-17 record descriptor identity, error propagation and empty shrink-only baselines. The permission-stat fallback question is dissolved because identity no longer selects a sidecar by pathname. ### `pnpm ci:remote:check` parses color-forced `gh` JSON and refuses a green remote

* **ID:** f-20261003-01 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** inline · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 1f678668-c21e-4c25-8200-a7808f5d4209
* **Where:** `scripts/check-remote-ci.mjs:59` (`parseJson`) and `:122-139` (`runsForBranch` runs `gh run list --json` and parses stdout as JSON). The same parse is used for `gh run view` at `:150-153`.
* **Defect:** The checker spawns `gh` with the parent environment. When `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` is set, `gh --json` writes ANSI into stdout even though the pipe is not a terminal. `JSON.parse` then throws and the checker exits 2 (`REFUSED: gh run list returned invalid JSON`). `FORCE_COLOR=1` alone does not. Measured 2026-10-03 with `gh run list --workflow Test --branch master --limit 1 --json conclusion`, each variable isolated: `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` wrote 108 bytes starting `\x1b[1;38m[\x1b[m` and gh's stderr was empty; `FORCE_COLOR=1` alone wrote 27 bytes, `[{"conclusion":"success"}]\n`, with no ANSI; `NO_COLOR=1` together with `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` and `FORCE_COLOR` unset still wrote those 108 ANSI bytes, stderr empty; both color variables unset wrote the 27-byte JSON array. A command that sets both cannot attribute the ANSI to `FORCE_COLOR`. Installed `gh` help and the official environment docs list `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `GH_FORCE_TTY`, and `NO_COLOR`, not `FORCE_COLOR`. The same command with both color variables unset returns a JSON array. A drain session's `pnpm ci:remote:check` before pushing `bfb7b901` exited 2 while the newest completed Test jobs were success; unsetting `FORCE_COLOR` and `CLICOLOR_FORCE` made the same check print `Remote CI check: OK` and exit 0. The `Path::exists` search-index sidecar entry is a different defect.
* **Why it matters:** A drain or any shell that exports `CLICOLOR_FORCE` cannot push. Exit 2 refuses the push, and the refusal names invalid JSON rather than a red job.
* **Proof:** From a clean checkout, `env CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 pnpm ci:remote:check` exits 2 and its stderr contains `gh run list returned invalid JSON`, while `env -u FORCE_COLOR -u CLICOLOR_FORCE pnpm ci:remote:check` exits 0 on the same green remote. `FORCE_COLOR=1` alone is not the trigger. After the fix, the `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` invocation parses `gh` output and exits 0 on that green remote, or exits 1 only when a completed Test job is actually red.
* **Related:** none in the ledger share this cause. `f-20260924-07` is the missing Windows type-check, not this parser.
* **Found by:** drain session `1f678668-c21e-4c25-8200-a7808f5d4209` while running `pnpm ci:remote:check` before the ordinary push of `bfb7b901`, 2026-10-03.
* **Handled:** commit "fix(gates): keep gh JSON uncoloured in ci:remote:check" (Grok Bot side lane, Codex leaf) spawns every `gh` call of `scripts/check-remote-ci.mjs` (`runChecked`: run list and run view) with a copy of the parent environment minus `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` and `GH_FORCE_TTY`, plus `NO_COLOR=1`. JSON parsing stays strict (no ANSI stripping); exit codes 0/1/2, the 30 s timeout and the buffer cap are unchanged.
* **Proof:** the new regression in `scripts/check-remote-ci-tests.mjs` failed before the fix (18 passed, 1 failed: "gh must receive an explicit environment") and passes after (19 passed). Local gh 2.45.0: `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 NO_COLOR=1` still wrote 108 bytes with ANSI, so removing `CLICOLOR_FORCE` is the operative change; the child environment wrote 27 bytes of plain JSON. Live on 2026-10-17, `env CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 node scripts/check-remote-ci.mjs` and the uncoloured run gave the identical verdict (a genuinely red completed `test` job on 244cfec5, exit 1) instead of exit 2 "invalid JSON". Review r1: correctness, root-cause, tests, minimalism, code-quality, error-handling all APPROVED.
* **Rejected:** stripping ANSI before `JSON.parse` would hide the cause and accept any colour-corrupted payload.

### Local frontend mutation counts static-mutant timeouts as kills, so it passed 100 % where CI found 23 survivors

* **ID:** f-20261003-04 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `stryker.config.mjs` (`thresholds.break: 100`, no `timeoutMS`/`timeoutFactor`, `ignoreStatic` unset, `concurrency` from `workerCount`), the `frontend-mutation` receipt gate in `scripts/run-push-gates.mjs` / `scripts/gate-receipt.mjs`, and the pre-review `frontend-mutation-changed-files` lane.
* **Defect:** Stryker scores a `Timeout` as detected. Static mutants (module-scope values such as the `annotationSchema` enum in `src/state/store/tabStorage.ts`) run the whole package suite per mutant, and under the local `agent-gate` scope with 21 runners they time out. On 2026-10-03 the workspace-storage package reported 100 % locally three times (pre-review on `2f4dc8c4`, `db20b0ec` and `fb69f852`, and `pnpm gates:push -- --frontend --rust` on `063080b9`). The local report `artifacts/mutation/frontend/workspace-storage/mutation.json` lists the 23 enum mutants at `tabStorage.ts:32-59` as `Timeout`. CI run 37127507309 (job 111215719788, same code at `ceafc21f`) ran each of them to completion: all 23 `Survived`, score 97.85, job red. The local gate is therefore a false green for any static mutant no test kills.
* **Why it matters:** the mutation gate is the only local proof that new tests actually constrain the code, and a push it passed reddened remote CI. The real test gap behind this instance is fixed in the f-20261001-12 repair; the gate defect remains.
* **Open question:** how a local run can tell a slow kill from a hidden survivor. Options: treat `Timeout` as a failure in the gate for static mutants, raise the timeout so static mutants finish, or run static mutants with fewer concurrent runners. The choice affects gate time and the `d-20261002-01` memory schedule.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, f-20261001-12 build run, 2026-10-03, after the remote Test job failed on `ceafc21f`. Related: f-20261001-12.
* **Proof:** a staged static mutant no test kills (for example the enum literal mutation above, with the f-20261001-12 repair test removed) must make the local `frontend-mutation` gate red, as it does on CI.
* **Why rejected:** Mutation timeout false-green; the CI backstop already catches survivors. Not worth fixing under universal rule 4d (only a defect with a cost is a finding; setup-findings triage 2026-10-13).

## 2026-10-04 — filed through the inbox spool

### The renderer tells listing failures apart by copying backend message literals, and nothing ties those copies to their Rust producers

* **ID:** f-20261003-05 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** bindings-ipc · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 7a491b7d-b9d5-4a75-9133-6e233e266d1b
* **Where:** the `f-20260913-05` plan's `listingFailurePresentation` (renderer, `src/components/common/`), which matches redacted `ErrorPayload` messages inside one backend category. The producers are `src-tauri/src/infra/path_authority/mod.rs` (`path authority is unavailable because its object changed`, `root changed concurrently`, `workspace is unavailable because its root changed`, `directory changed while resolving`, `verified identity does not match registration target`, `{noun} root changed; select it again`), `src-tauri/src/infra/fs.rs` `check_directory_listing_bound` (`directory listing exceeded {limit} entries`) and `src-tauri/src/file_workspace.rs` (`workspace listing exceeded {MAX_WORKSPACE_LISTING_DEPTH} levels`). The payload shape is `src-tauri/src/error.rs` (`ErrorPayload { tag, category, message }`) and `src/platform/errors.ts` `normalizeError`.
* **Defect:** `conflict` and `resource-limit` each cover failures that need different user instructions: a replaced root versus a poisoned authority, and an over-bound root versus a full path registry. The payload carries no field that tells them apart, so the `f-20260913-05` plan matches the full redacted message against copied literals. Its tests feed those copies through `normalizeError` and through mocked IPC. No test ties a copy to its Rust producer: the bound's serialization test checks only `category` and `tag` (`infra/fs.rs`), and the depth test checks only the variant. If a producer rewords its message, that failure silently falls back to the retry sentence, and every planned test stays green.
* **Why it matters:** `f-20260830-08` removed substring classification so that the renderer would classify on what the backend sends. Exact matching inside one category brings back message-text coupling for eight strings. A silent fallback re-creates the `f-20260913-05` defect: "please try again" for a root that retrying cannot fix.
* **Open question:** how does the backend give the renderer a stable listing-failure reason without an eighth `AppErrorCategory` (`d-20260901-34`, `d-20260904-06`)? Options: (a) an optional machine-readable `reason` field on `ErrorPayload`, set by the listing producers and regenerated through Specta; (b) dedicated `Error` variants mapped onto the existing backend categories, with a reason code carried in the payload; (c) keep message matching and add a producer-consumer proof, either a Rust test that pins each producer's exact message or a generated constant table shared by both sides. (a) and (b) change the IPC contract and the generated bindings; (c) keeps the coupling but makes it visible.
* **Related:** `f-20260913-05` (the consumer; its plan review records this as I16 and keeps the copied literals as a known limit), `f-20260830-08` (handled; removed substring classification), `f-20260913-06` (handled; added the bound), `d-20261003-05`, `d-20261003-12`.
* **Found by:** Codex `review-tests` lens, round 6 of the `f-20260913-05` PLAN-REFRESH plan review (`tasks/plans/2026-10-03-listing-failure-copy.md`), 2026-10-03; the numeric half was raised by `review-error-handling` in the same round and is fixed in that plan by anchored templates.
* **Closed 2026-10-04 (drain session 648a7fac-1f9b-4bc0-8e9a-df298dc5f16d, records review of the f-20260914-05 push):** already resolved by `dccd9636` (feat(errors): label listing failures of the chosen root with rootFailure) and `20ae3a5a` (feat(files,databases): tell the user why a listing failed and offer re-selection), under `d-20261003-22`. The backend now sends a typed `rootFailure` label on `ErrorPayload` (`src-tauri/src/error.rs`, serialization pinned by the test around line 472-479), and `src/components/files/listingFailure.ts` classifies only that label (`visible.rootFailure`), with no message-text matching. The open question's option (a)/(b) was taken; the copied-literal coupling this finding describes no longer exists. The entry was merged open by the drain's between-cluster inbox merge `9d6c4d99`, after its fix had landed.

### ChessFable's push skill does not name the install end detail at its installer step, so a queued drain can withhold the checkout-available card

* **ID:** f-20261003-06 · **Status:** rejected · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** inline · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `.claude/skills/push/SKILL.md:387-393` (the `master`-only `bash scripts/install-local.sh` step) and its stage-emission section at `:19-30`.
* **Defect:** Since agent-kit 5327fa6..25cfdce (pushed and released 2026-10-03), a drain under `--queue-plans` sends the persistent "Implementation finished — checkout available" card only when the latest `push` stage ended with exactly `install verified` (the installer ran for this push and succeeded) or `install not applicable` (the skill does not install for this push — here: any branch other than `master`), and shows `Waiting for CI` only when the stage detail is `waiting for required CI`. The shared contract is `~/.claude/references/push-review-policy.md` → "Caller contract for explicit stage emissions", which this skill already reads first (`:9`), so a session that follows it emits the details; this skill's own installer step and CI wait do not name them, so a session that follows only the local text ends `push` without either detail and the drain withholds the card (fail-safe, never a false announcement).
* **Why it matters:** ChessFable is where the missing checkout-available notice was observed (2026-10-01); without the detail at the installer step, Felix waits on a checkout that is already free.
* **Proof:** after the fix, the skill text contains, at the CI wait, `drain_stage start push "waiting for required CI"` and a fresh `push` start once the result is known, and at the installer step `drain_stage end push "install verified"` after `scripts/install-local.sh` succeeds on `master`, `drain_stage end push "install not applicable"` on any other branch, and a failure-naming end detail when the installer fails; `grep -F 'install verified' .claude/skills/push/SKILL.md` and `grep -F 'install not applicable' .claude/skills/push/SKILL.md` both match.
* **Related:** agent-kit plan `tasks/plans/2026-10-02-checkout-available-notification.md` (issues I11, I16, I18) and decision `d-20261003-20` in agent-kit's `tasks/decisions.md`.
* **Found by:** Claude Code, agent-kit build session 8ad6026e-e969-46a2-bdf8-dbb0ae99964f (kit-consumers lens, plan-review rounds 5-7), 2026-10-03.
* **Why rejected:** Drain stage-detail wording. Not worth fixing under universal rule 4d (only a defect with a cost is a finding; setup-findings triage 2026-10-13).
