### The Annotate editor's Markdown save can still change a comment: literal delimiters next to authored marks, adjacent links merged

* **ID:** f-20261013-02 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 92629247-30b0-484a-a451-64fd78836bcb
* **Impact class:** data-loss
* **Where:** `src/components/panels/annotation/AnnotationEditor.tsx` (the save path `onUpdate` → `editor.getMarkdown()` at ~:169 and the synchronisation comparison at ~:186; the serializer overrides `CommentMarkdown`, `CommentStarterKit` doc/paragraph/link `renderMarkdown` and the `Underline.extend` renderer), `@tiptap/markdown` 3.20.0 mark-boundary helpers (`node_modules/@tiptap/markdown/src/utils.ts:34`, `:50` compare mark types without attributes), the shared lexer `src/utils/commentMarkdown.ts`, `src/utils/pgnComment.ts` (`COMMENT_UNDERLINE`).
* **Defect:** the editor serializes its document through tiptap's Markdown renderer plus local overrides and never checks that the saved Markdown reads back as the same text and marks. Measured by the f-20261001-10 push review (closure round 5, review-correctness, source-traced, confidence 99, reproduced by a read-only probe in the follow-up judgment): (1) load literal `a++bc` and underline only `c` → saved `a++b++c++`, which the shared lexer reads as `abc++` with `b` underlined; (2) load `[a](https://a.test)[b](https://b.test)` and type `!` → saved `[ab](https://b.test)!`, so `a` silently points at `b`'s destination. The judgment also measured an unmarked literal `**x**` typed in the editor reloading as bold `x`. Classes (1) and (2) predate f-20261001-10 (stock tiptap writes the same strings); they are filed here because the f-20261001-10 run's plan bounded the editor's byte-identical round trip to its own case list (plan obligation O2), and a general lossless serializer is a separate design.
* **Failure scenario:** a user annotates a ChessBase comment that contains `++` (double check) or two adjacent links and applies underline or edits nearby; the saved comment shows different text or a link to the wrong place in the notation and in every exported PGN.
* **Open question:** what does the editor show for a backslash escape (today the notation decodes `1\.` to `1.` while the editor shows and keeps `1\.`, d-20261013-17), and once that is one semantic text contract, which mark coverage may an owned serializer drop when the dialect cannot express it — versus failing the save closed and keeping the draft?
* **Fix shape (from the focused fresh-context review-plan judgment, verdict REVISE on the narrower question, recorded verbatim in `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-13-comment-dialect-and-inline-flow-review.md` → "Serializer judgment"):** decide one escape contract first (supersede the escape-display wording of d-20261013-17); then own the dialect serializer in a focused utility beside `commentMarkdown.ts` (paragraphs, hard breaks, text, bold/italic/strike/underline/link; links compared by `(href, title)`; literal syntax escaped independently of formatting; balanced runs); gate the real save boundary with a semantic check (reparse with the production adapters, compare flattened text and per-position mark coverage including link attributes; on mismatch keep the draft and report, never silently drop expressible formatting) and use the same serializer for the synchronisation comparison; add property-style round-trip tests over generated mark layouts with explicit seeds for authored whitespace/newline underline, literal `a++b` + underlined `c`, adjacent differently attributed links, unmarked `**x**`, removed URL links, escaped delimiters and linked whitespace under underline. Rejected there: per-case fixes, a guard that drops marks down to plain text (plain text is still parsed as Markdown), removing underline authoring (conflicts with d-20261013-09 and leaves the link and literal-text classes).
* **Related:** f-20261001-10 (handled by the same run; its handoff above carries the full review history — load it before plan review), decisions d-20261013-09, d-20261013-16, d-20261013-17.
* **Found by:** Claude Code (Opus 5.5), drain build run for f-20261001-10 (session 92629247-30b0-484a-a451-64fd78836bcb), push-review closure round 5 and the follow-up serializer judgment.

The Annotate save now goes through `src/utils/commentSerializer.ts`. `compareCommentDocument` checks the editor document against the editor Markdown parse and `parseNotationComment`. A mismatch or a throw refuses the save, does not call `setComment`, keeps the draft, keeps the stored comment, and shows `Board.Annotate.SaveFailed`.

Decoded escapes show in the notation and in the editor (d-20261018-08). A save may drop only the underline coverage listed in d-20261018-09. An underline that contains `++` stays underlined when `++a\+\+b++` reparses (d-20261018-10). Opening a comment does not rewrite it. An equivalent stored spelling does not replace the open document.

Proof before the close: pre-review was green on `cc29b063`. `pnpm test:e2e:container --project=workspace-tabs` passed 7 tests and wrote no snapshot diff. The refusal alert is the unstyled `[role="alert"]` in the Annotate panel; the mounted editor test asserts its text is the translation key. Review record: `tasks/handoffs/2026-10-18-f-20261013-02-review.md`.

### Rust build output is never evicted, so the checkout and drain-worktree target directories grow by 10-17 GB per busy day

* **ID:** f-20261017-04 · **Status:** open · **Area:** gate-scripts · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Where:** `src-tauri/target/` in the main checkout and in every worktree that runs the Rust gates (`chessfable.worktrees/drain/src-tauri/target/`), plus `mutants.out/backend/cargo-target/`. Written by the gate scripts that drive cargo: `scripts/gate-receipt.mjs`, `scripts/rust-branch-coverage.mjs` / `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` (`llvm-cov-target`), `scripts/run-backend-mutation.mjs` (`mutants.out`). No script, gate or drain step ever removes stale artifacts.
* **Defect:** cargo keeps every artifact for every dependency version, feature set and profile it has ever built, and nothing in the project evicts them. Measured on tuxedo-atlas 2026-10-17: main checkout `src-tauri/target` 123 GB (`debug/incremental` 56 GB across 86 crate-session directories, `debug/deps` 22 GB of which 3,640 files date from August and 2,743 from September, `llvm-cov-target` 23 GB, cross targets 13 GB). `chessfable.worktrees/drain/src-tauri/target` 32 GB, all written since 2026-10-14 (17.3 GB on 10-14, 6.9 GB on 10-16, 14.1 GB on 10-17). `mutants.out` 6.9 GB, plus an 8 GB copy of a target under `/tmp/catalog-engine-phase1-20261016/snapshot`. The main target wrote 12.1 GB on 10-11 and 9.1 GB on 10-13. Together that is about 160 GB on a root filesystem that ran full on 2026-10-12 (from a different cause, agent-kit `f-20261012-10`). It has no ceiling. sccache (`~/.cache/sccache`, 5.6 GB) is already present, so a cold rebuild after eviction costs less than a cold build without it.
* **Open question:** where eviction lives and what it keeps. Options include: delete a worktree's `target/` when its build/drain run lands; evict artifacts not used for N days in long-lived targets (main checkout, the reused `drain` worktree) from a gate wrapper; cap total size; or share one target directory per profile across worktrees. The plan must weigh warm-cache gate times (measured before and after) against the bound, and decide whether the worktree half belongs here or in agent-kit's worktree lifecycle.
* **Proof:** after one week of normal drain activity with the fix in place, `du -sh` of every ChessFable `target/` and `mutants.out` stays under the chosen bound, and warm gate timings stay within the measured baseline.
* **Found by:** Felix noticed the tower's disk growing again; disk investigation from a `~` session on 2026-10-17.
* **Impact class:** tooling

### Linked player rename rewrites an entire physical line and can drop unrelated PGN tags

* **ID:** f-20261020-02 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** pgn-import · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 7328103f-da3c-4f90-9686-4abe6e2beeb1
* **Impact class:** data-loss
* **Follow-up of:** f-20261004-15
* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/db/linked_collections.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/linked_collections/tests.rs`.
* **Defect:** The unpublished linked player-rename implementation reads physical lines. For a legal line containing `[White "Alice"] [Black "Bob"]`, IdentityPlayerHeaders keeps the final name Bob, while the replacement key is selected from the line's White prefix. Renaming Bob can therefore replace the whole line with a White tag and drop Black. Renaming Alice on that line does nothing. Leading whitespace also bypasses the matching prefixes. This is confirmed by the production callback and replacement source trace, with a genuine parser/runtime regression still required.
* **Change:** Locate and replace only the matching White or Black tag value through the existing PGN parsing/scanning boundary. Preserve every unrelated byte, tag, comment and movetext section. Do not reconstruct a whole game from database columns or infer player roles from physical-line starts.
* **Proof:** Production linked rename fixtures with both player tags on one line, whitespace, escapes, BOM and CRLF must update only the selected player and preserve unrelated bytes. Reverse the production fix with tests retained, observe the matching preservation assertion fail, restore byte-identically and rerun linked native tests.
* **Review lens:** review-pgn-index.
* **Related:** f-20261004-05 is a distinct existing scanner boundary defect for multiple tag pairs on one line. The rename defect is in the new transformation, and both paths need examination without conflating their causes. The pending Home-alias filing concerns renderer grouping, a separate cause.
* **Found by:** Root source inspection during integrated proof. Plan authorship and arbitration shared one context. Detection ran on the same OpenAI model family as the code.

Linked player-tag edits preserve unrelated tags on the same physical PGN line and use the canonical scanner/tag-boundary contract.

### The shared-deadline revocation test blocks on its second accept when the first request uses the budget

* **ID:** f-20261026-03 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** oauth-credentials · **Root:** - · **Entry:** build · **Blocked:** none
* **Filed from:** 12100003-de22-488c-b30e-133be7529fc8

* **Where:** `src-tauri/src/oauth.rs:1611-1642`, test `oauth::tests::production_revocation_uses_one_absolute_deadline_for_both_requests_and_reads`. The panic is the `timeout(...).await.unwrap()` at line 1642.
* **Defect:** The test server accepts a revocation, sleeps 60ms, answers 401, then blocks on a second `accept` for the token-test. The client uses one 120ms deadline for both requests. When the first request consumes that budget, the client never opens the second connection, the server waits forever, and the 2s outer `tokio::time::timeout` returns `Elapsed(())`. The unwrap panics before the `Unreachable` assertion. Observed on the newest completed `rust-macos-test`: Test run 40251763823, job 121345009122, head `0049b7f981c59513ffeaf89c5329647b91974c90`, completed 2026-10-26T01:08:48Z. The job log says the test panicked at `src/oauth.rs:1642:10` with `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Elapsed(())`. 2760 passed, 1 failed, 1 ignored, finished in 247.59s. The step was "Run Rust tests". This is not a wrong `Unreachable` assertion. `pnpm ci:remote:check` on 2026-10-26 exits 1 on that job and blocks the f-20261006-07 push. Those commits do not touch `oauth.rs` and do not repair this test. Not reproduced locally. The production `REVOCATION_TIMEOUT` of 30s is asserted at the start of the test and is not what elapsed.
* **Spotted outside diff:** review range `0049b7f981c59513ffeaf89c5329647b91974c90..653f652d8491e681904dcd3a2515b34523c6d3d9` does not change `src-tauri/src/oauth.rs`.
* **Failure scenario:** A macOS `cargo test` of this binary reaches the shared-deadline revocation test while the first loopback request is slow enough to exhaust the 120ms budget. The server blocks on the second accept, the 2s watchdog elapses, and `rust-macos-test` fails. `pnpm ci:remote:check` then refuses later pushes.
* **Open question:** How should this test prove that one absolute deadline covers both the revocation request and the token-test read when the first request already consumes the 120ms budget? The server must not block forever on the second accept, and the fix must not widen the production 30s `REVOCATION_TIMEOUT` or weaken the 120ms shared-budget assertion.
* **Proof:** On a tree that still has the blocking second `accept`, delaying the first response past 120ms makes `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin chessfable production_revocation_uses_one_absolute_deadline_for_both_requests_and_reads -- --exact` panic with `Elapsed(())`. After the repair the same delay reaches `assert_eq!(outcome, LichessRevocationOutcome::Unreachable)` and the process exits 0. The hosted witness is run 40251763823 job 121345009122.
* **Related:** f-20261004-04 added this shared-deadline outcome. f-20261011-03 tracks other wall-clock `Elapsed(())` failures under local gate pressure. This one is the server blocking on `accept`, not that gate-design question. f-20261008-05 is credential removal, not this test.

* **Found by:** Grok, drain session 12100003-de22-488c-b30e-133be7529fc8, push of f-20261006-07, 2026-10-26. Job log retained at `/tmp/f-20261006-07-lenses/macos-job.log.zip` (UTF-8 text, not a zip).

* **ID:** f-20261029-09 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** e2e-gate · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none

* **Impact class:** behaviour

Both failures: `[data-notation-current="true"] button` not found within 8000 ms. Preview-scope cases passed. Nf3 d6) 2. Bc4 Nc6. So after the user clicked a move, the tree position was reset to the root although the moves remain. The test clicks immediately after `d6` becomes visible, so an asynchronous step of opening the game (load, file-freshness or persistence replay) apparently replaces the tree state after the first user navigation. Not yet confirmed from the trace (trace.zip in the same artifact).
* **Failure scenario:** a user opens a game from the library and clicks a move at once; a late state replacement resets the board to the start position. In CI it makes the required `test` job red intermittently and blocks pushes (ci:remote:check refusal).
* **Related findings:** f-20261019-08 (handled, notation context menu closing before pointer clicks; same spec, different cause: menu lifetime, not tree position). No shared Root.
* **Proof:** a discriminating repro (e.g. delay the game-open completion in the e2e mock and click before it lands) that fails before the fix and passes after; then `pnpm test:e2e:container --project=engine-gap --grep 'notation-delete:'` green repeatedly. Do not raise the timeout or add a sleep to mask it.
* **Pickup re-check (2026-10-29):** Already repaired by be05fbfd, the published form of 9736068a, under d-20261029-07 and handled f-20261029-02. Both reported revisions, 9b76350b and 291d7fb2, predate the destination Info-tab wait. Current setupNotationMenu waits for that workspace-only control before locating or clicking notation. No production source change is warranted by this finding.
* **Trace evidence:** Independently downloaded original failed-attempt browser artifact 12904612511 from run 40886841564, retained at /tmp/chessfable-f-20261029-09/hosted-audit-second.zip. In workspace inline trace c012c, Nc6 click call@128 starts at 26367.553 ms and targets preview coordinates x=1151.78,y=686.67. The 26558.009 ms frame still shows Library with Nc6 selected. The 27832.758 ms frame shows the newly mounted workspace at its initial position and the e5 context menu. In workspace table trace e94e9, call@128 starts at 26449.592 ms and targets preview coordinates x=1319.36,y=686.67. The 26288.426 ms frame still shows Library and the 27445.701 ms frame shows the new workspace. These are separate preview and workspace trees, not evidence of a reset inside an already mounted workspace. The original production-reset interpretation is superseded by these traces.
* **Source confirmation:** openFile awaits read and parse, createTab synchronously seeds the completed tree before publishing the tab, and FileCard navigates only after openFile returns. Tab-tree storage reads are synchronous. Freshness is marked verified before navigation, FileFreshnessGate hides children until verified, and an unchanged stamp does not replace the tree. A separate read-only Codex leaf independently traced the same path and found no evidenced second reset.
* **Disposition:** Close as an overlapping report of the already handled synchronization defect, governed by d-20261029-07. Preserve the existing workspace wait and every current-move, pointer, subtree and screenshot assertion. Reject adding a sleep, raising a timeout, retrying the click or changing production tree behavior without evidence. No new technical decision, product change or source edit. Plan authorship and arbitration shared one root context. Detection ran on the same model family as the code, in a separate leaf context.

* **ID:** f-20261029-07 · **Status:** handled · **Area:** frontend-ui · **Root:** - · **Entry:** lens · **Blocked:** none
* **Impact class:** behaviour
* **Where:** src/components/panels/analysis/TablebaseInfo.tsx:22 sorts `data.moves` with `compareTablebaseMoves` (lines 98-103) using `tablebaseRank` (lines 86-95), which ranks `win` first and `loss` last.
* **Defect:** Each tablebase move's `category` describes the position after the move, from the opponent's side; the same file acknowledges this by passing the inverted `turn` to `OutcomeBadge` (line 72). * **Open question:** none beyond confirming the response semantics; the fix is to rank child categories from the mover's perspective (child `loss` first, then `blessed-loss`, `draw`, `cursed-win`, `win`), keeping the SAN tie-break.
* **Proof:** A unit test of `compareTablebaseMoves` (or of the rendered order) with child categories `loss`, `draw` and `win` asserting the `loss` move first, red before the fix.
* **Found by:** Codex review-correctness lens, ChessRiddle design build, 2026-10-29.
* **Handled:** Corrected the known child-category ranks in commit `69ab4044` under d-20261029-31. Child loss now sorts first, then blessed-loss, draw, cursed-win and win. The existing SAN tie-break, uncertain-category fallback, cached-data copy, badge perspective and move interactions are preserved.
* **Verified:** Eighteen TablebaseInfo unit tests pass. With only the production fix stashed and the new tests retained, seven regression tests fail, then all eighteen pass after restoration. The pinned container browser journey displays all nine move cards in the corrected order and plays the winning queen promotion through the renderer. No committed screenshot baseline changed. Screenshot: /tmp/chessfable-f-20261029-07/tablebase-browser.png.
* **Pre-review proof:** `pnpm checks:pre-review` exited 0 on the final source and test changes. Both selected mutation packages scored 100. The corrected run's completion record is /home/felixb/.claude/drain-state/drain-90a2aa88.d/gates-b91e801f-c97a-4308-823b-d8d1bc2de01a/gate-pre-review-corrected.fyYsec/completion.record. The earlier interrupted attempt is not passing proof.
* **Response semantics confirmed:** A recorded response from the actual product endpoint, tablebase.lichess.org/standard, has parent win, h8=Q+ child loss, Kg8 draw and Kf6 child win. The Rust command preserves the response body. Evidence: /tmp/chessfable-f-20261029-07/product-endpoint-response.json.
* **Rejected alternative:** Dropping the comparator and using provider order would also change the existing SAN tie-break, beyond the perspective correction.
